templates.name: Exit interview guide (HRBP-led)
templates.purpose: A structured 30-45 minute conversation, led by an HRBP outside the reporting line, to understand why a valued employee is leaving and what would have kept them. It produces coded, comparable data for attrition analysis and routes any misconduct allegation to Employee Relations instead of leaving it in exit notes.
templates.audience: HRBPs and People Partners who conduct the interviews; HR Analytics, who code and report results; Employee Relations, who receive any allegations.
templates.when: Between notice day +3 and the final week (not the last day); by phone within 30 days of exit if missed. Required for regrettable leavers, director level and above, and teams with 2+ exits in 6 months; the anonymous exit survey covers everyone else.
templates.owner: HR Business Partners (conduct); HR Analytics (coding and reporting)

sections.title: Preparation & opening
sections.intro: Complete the checks before booking. Read the opening lines close to verbatim: they set confidentiality expectations you must be able to keep.

items.text: Confirm the leaver has received the anonymous exit survey (T-EXIT-SURVEY) link; the interview adds depth but does not replace it.

Pull context from Darwinbox: tenure, level, last two ratings, compa-ratio, last increase and promotion dates, unvested equity value and next vest date, manager and skip-level, and team attrition over the last 12 months.
items.detail: Use this to probe, not to argue. Do not quote pay data back to the employee.

items.text: Confirm you are outside the employee's reporting line and not involved in any open ER case about them; ask ER about open cases, leave or accommodation files and recent complaints.
items.detail: If there is open protected activity, brief ER before the interview and be ready to use the allegations protocol.

items.text: Book 45 minutes in a private room or on video (camera optional) between notice day +3 and the final week, never during asset return on the last day. Offer Mandarin in Taiwan and China, with an interpreter who is not a co-worker.

Thanks for making time. This conversation is about learning from your experience so we can improve things for the people who stay. It isn't about changing your mind, and nothing you say will affect your final pay, benefits, equity, references or rehire eligibility.

I'll take notes. What you share is reported to leadership as themes, without your name, and only when there are enough responses that you can't be identified. If you want something passed on with your name on it, tell me and I'll do that only with your OK.

There's one exception. If you tell me about harassment, discrimination, retaliation, safety, fraud or any other possible breach of the law or our Code, I have to pass it to the right team so it can be looked into. I'll tell you if that happens.
You can skip any question. Nothing in this conversation limits your right to contact or file a complaint with any government agency, such as the SEC, EEOC, NLRB or a local labor authority.
In a sentence or two, how would you describe your time here?
items.detail: Warm-up. Note the tone and the first topic they raise; it is often the real reason.

items.text: What was the main reason you started looking, or said yes to another opportunity?
items.detail: Probe: 'When did you first start thinking about leaving? What was happening then?' Code the primary reason and whether it was push (something here), pull (something there) or both.

items.text: Was there a specific moment or event that tipped the decision?
items.detail: Common triggers: a reorg or manager change, a missed promotion, the comp review outcome, a cancelled project or program, a return-to-office change, layoff anxiety, or a vest date passing.

items.text: Were you actively looking, or did someone approach you?
items.detail: If approached, ask how (recruiter, former colleague, agency) but not who. Repeated approaches to one team by the same firm are a signal for TA and Security.

items.text: What other reasons played a part, even small ones?
items.detail: Capture up to three secondary codes.

items.text: If you could have changed one thing about your job, what would have made the biggest difference?
How would you describe your working relationship with your manager?
items.detail: Probe: clarity of expectations, how often you had 1:1s, recognition, support when things went wrong. Ask for a rating from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) and record it.

items.text: How useful was the feedback you got on your work? When did you last have a real conversation about your career?
Did you see a realistic path to your next level here? What was in the way?
items.detail: Probe: clarity of promotion criteria, calibration outcomes, sponsorship, and scope available on the team.

items.text: Did you look at internal moves before deciding to leave? What happened?
items.detail: If a manager blocked or discouraged an internal move, code 'Internal mobility blocked'. It is a strong signal and fixable.

items.text: Were you working on the technology and projects you wanted to work on?
items.detail: For engineers, probe node and technology choices, ownership of blocks or tapeouts, influence on architecture, and time spent on maintenance versus new design.

items.text: How did you feel about your pay compared with what you could get elsewhere?
items.detail: Then, only if they are comfortable: 'How does the new package compare, including base, bonus, equity and sign-on?' Record as a band (within 10%, 10-25% higher, more than 25% higher). It is voluntary; do not press.

items.text: How did equity factor into your decision: refresh grants, vesting timing, share price?
items.detail: Code 'Pay: equity' if awards are underwater or there is a refresh gap. Note if the resignation followed a vest date or a missed refresh.

items.text: How sustainable was your workload: hours, on-call, tapeout crunches, late calls with other time zones?
items.detail: If an employee in Taiwan, China or India describes unrecorded overtime or regular after-hours calls, note it and send it to People Ops/Payroll for review; it can create back-pay liability.

items.text: Did hybrid, remote or return-to-office arrangements play a part?
Did tools, lab time, EDA licenses or compute limit your work?
Did you feel you could raise concerns or disagree without negative consequences?
Did you feel included and treated fairly on your team, in assignments, recognition and promotions?
items.detail: General answers are feedback. If they describe unfair treatment linked to a protected characteristic, or retaliation, switch to the allegations protocol.

sections.title: Destination & what would have kept them

items.text: Where are you going, and in what kind of role? You don't have to tell me.
items.detail: Voluntary. Record only the employer category: competitor, customer, foundry/OSAT/EDA partner, startup, large tech, academia, not disclosed. Never ask what they will work on beyond the title.

items.text: Competitor or customer destinations: don't debate the choice, apply pressure or discuss the details of the new role. Notify Legal and Security the same day under the departing-employee protocol (ER-10). For customers, also tell the account's sales leader so coverage can be planned.

As a reminder, your confidentiality and invention obligations continue after you leave. If any company material is on a personal device or account, let's get it returned or deleted before your last day. Security can help with that.
What would have kept you? Is there anything we could have done, now or six months ago, that would have changed your decision?
items.detail: If a regretted leaver signals they are still open to staying, say you'll pass it on, make no promises, and escalate the same day to the HRBP lead and skip-level under the counteroffer process (CO-05).

items.text: Would you consider coming back in the future? What would need to be true?
On a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend [Company] to a friend as a place to work?
items.detail: eNPS: 9-10 promoter, 7-8 passive, 0-6 detractor.

sections.title: Regrettable-loss signals
sections.intro: Complete after the interview. Two or more signals means a regrettable loss: flag it to the HRBP lead and the talent review (PD-05).

items.text: Last two ratings in the top two bands, or on a promotion-ready list.

Holds a critical or scarce skill (e.g., analog/mixed-signal, physical design sign-off, DFT, post-silicon validation lead, SerDes/PHY, security architecture) or a key customer relationship (FAE, account lead).
Named successor or on a succession slate, or sole owner of a block, flow, tool or customer program on a current tapeout or release.
Backfill expected to take more than 90 days, or to cost more than 20% above the leaver's current pay.
Leaving for a direct competitor or customer, or recruited as part of a group from the same team.
Preventable: the primary reason was within the company's control (manager, growth, pay position, workload, blocked mobility).

sections.title: Allegations protocol
sections.intro: Use this when the employee describes harassment, discrimination, retaliation, threats or violence, safety hazards, fraud or accounting issues, bribery, export-control or trade-secret breaches, or wage-hour violations.

items.text: Thank you for telling me. This needs to be looked at properly, so I'm going to pause the regular questions and make sure it gets to the right team.

Stop the exit questions. Do not investigate, cross-examine, judge credibility or promise an outcome. Record in the employee's words: what, who, when, where, witnesses, documents, and whether it was reported before.
Do not promise confidentiality. Explain that the information will be shared only with the people who need it to deal with the concern.

Route within 1 business day through case management (ER-01): conduct and harassment to Employee Relations; accounting, audit or securities concerns to Ethics & Compliance for audit committee reporting; export-control issues to Trade Compliance; threats to Security immediately.

Apply local routes: sexual harassment complaints by women in India go to the Internal Committee (POSH Act); in Taiwan, sexual harassment and workplace bullying complaints follow the statutory complaint procedures; in Ontario, complaints go through the OHSA harassment program.

Do not change or delay the separation date, final pay or any separation offer because of the allegation. Tell Legal the same day if a separation agreement is pending or rehire eligibility is being decided.

Someone from Employee Relations will contact you within two business days. You can also use the Speak Up line at any time, including after you leave, and you can always go to a government agency directly.
Thank you, this is genuinely useful. Is there anything I didn't ask that you'd want leadership to hear?
Offer the alumni network and ask whether they agree to be contacted about future roles. Record the consent separately, with the date.
items.detail: Keep consent separate from the interview notes (CCPA, PIPL, DPDP, PDPA).

items.text: Primary reason code (one)
items.detail: Pay: base | Pay: equity/refresh | Career growth/promotion | Manager relationship | Work content/technology | Workload/burnout | Flexibility/location/RTO | Culture/inclusion | Org change/uncertainty | Relocation/family/personal | Further study | Recruited away (pull only) | Other

items.text: Secondary reason codes (up to three), and push / pull / both
Regrettable (Y/N) and preventable (Yes / Maybe / No), with a one-line rationale
Destination category, and date Legal/Security were notified (competitor, customer or controlled-technology access)
Manager rating (1-5) and eNPS (0-10)
Allegation raised (Y/N), case ID, where it was routed, date
Feedback the employee agreed to share under their name, verbatim, and who receives it
Recommended actions, each with an owner and due date
items.detail: E.g., pay review for peers at the same level, manager coaching, a mobility policy fix. Enter notes in the Darwinbox exit module (restricted access) within 2 business days.

notes: The interviewer must sit outside the leaver's reporting line; if the HRBP works closely with the manager, swap with an HRBP from a neighboring group.
An exit interview is neither an investigation nor a negotiation. Allegations go to ER; retention attempts go through the counteroffer process (CO-05), never ad hoc promises.
Write down what was said, not your view of the manager or the employee's credibility. Exit notes are discoverable and subject to personnel-file and data-access requests.
Report themes only where at least 5 responses exist; show a manager-level trend only after 3+ exits from that manager.
Pair with the anonymous exit survey (T-EXIT-SURVEY): the survey gives coverage, the interview gives depth on regretted and strategic leavers.
Never use exit-interview content to mark someone ineligible for rehire without an ER review.
Hold the interview in the local language and translate verbatim quotes for the record.

countryNotes.us: Nothing in the interview may discourage agency reporting (SEC Rule 21F-17, NLRA Section 7). Protected complaints raised at exit go to ER before any later decision such as rehire eligibility or references.
countryNotes.us-ca: Former employees can request their personnel file (LC 1198.5) and make CCPA access requests, so treat exit notes as disclosable. Marking someone 'not eligible for rehire' within 90 days of a complaint raised here carries a retaliation presumption (LC 98.6, 1102.5).
countryNotes.ca: Ontario harassment complaints raised at exit must still be investigated under the OHSA program, with both parties told the results in writing. BC PIPA requires notice of the purpose for collecting exit data.
countryNotes.in: Sexual harassment disclosures by women go to the Internal Committee (POSH Act; complaint within 3 months, extendable by 3). Collect alumni-contact consent separately now, ahead of DPDP duties starting 13 May 2027.
countryNotes.tw: Sexual harassment disclosures trigger the Gender Equality in Employment Act complaint process and notice to the local authority. Bullying disclosures (OSH Act chapter, from 1 July 2026) must be investigated and registered in MOL's system even after the employee leaves.
countryNotes.cn: Hold the interview in Mandarin under a PIPL notice, and don't move identifiable notes to US systems without a cross-border basis and separate consent. Confirm the non-compete activation or release decision has been given in writing.

templates.name: Offboarding checklist
templates.purpose: One checklist, sorted by owner, to exit an employee cleanly: correct pay on time in every jurisdiction, assets and IP recovered, access removed and every required document issued. Day offsets (D = last day of employment) let Darwinbox generate and track each task automatically.
templates.audience: People Ops/HRBP (orchestrator), managers, departing employees, Payroll, Stock Admin, Benefits, IT, Security, Facilities, Legal, Trade Compliance.
templates.when: Triggered when a termination is entered in Darwinbox (resignation accepted or involuntary decision approved). For involuntary exits, D-14 to D-1 tasks collapse to the day of the meeting.
templates.owner: People Ops (process owner); each lane owns and evidences its own items

items.text: Submit your resignation in Darwinbox with a proposed last day, and confirm your notice period under your contract or local law.
items.detail: Taiwan: 10/20/30 days by tenure. China: 30 days (3 in probation). India: per contract, usually 60-90 days. No statutory resignation notice in the US or under the ON/BC ESAs.

items.text: Agree a knowledge-transfer plan with your manager covering in-flight work, design databases, scripts, test benches, lab setups and customer commitments.
Submit final expense reports and any outstanding reimbursement claims.
Update your personal email, mailing address and phone in Darwinbox and the equity platform so tax forms, benefits notices and equity messages reach you.
Remove personal files from company devices. Do not delete company data, and do not copy company files to personal devices, USB drives, personal email or cloud storage.
Complete the exit survey, and attend the exit interview if one is scheduled.
Return your laptop, badge, tokens, phone, lab equipment, evaluation boards, engineering samples and notebooks, and sign the return-of-property and confidentiality certification.
Note your equity deadlines (exercise window for vested options, usually 90 days; ESPP refund) and keep your equity-platform login active.
Acknowledge the resignation within 1 business day and tell the HRBP. Do not make or hint at a counteroffer without HRBP and Total Rewards (CO-05).
Flag departure risk to the HRBP: joining a competitor or customer, access to controlled technology or crown-jewel design data, recent unusual downloads.
items.detail: This triggers the departing-employee path (ER-10): early access review, possible garden leave and an exit certification.

items.text: Finalize the knowledge-transfer plan and reassign owners for repositories, design blocks, test plans, lab assets, customer accounts and approval workflows.
Decide whether to backfill or restructure; if backfilling, submit a requisition justification (T-REQ).
Confirm final commission, bonus, on-call and shift data with Payroll (sales, FAE and lab shift roles).
Tell the team and key customers using the agreed message; give no reason for the departure.
Confirm asset return, remove the employee from approval chains and distribution lists, and transfer ownership of documents and drives.
Accept the resignation in writing and confirm the last day; for involuntary exits, confirm approvals and meeting prep (T-TERM-SCRIPT).
items.detail: India: fixing the last working day starts the 2-working-day full-and-final clock. Taiwan and China: acceptance isn't legally required, but confirm the date in writing.

items.text: Enter the termination in Darwinbox with reason code and effective date, which triggers IT, Payroll, Benefits and Stock Admin tasks.
Run the holds check: open ER case, legal hold (ER-09), leave or accommodation, visa sponsorship, non-compete decision.
items.detail: H-1B: withdraw the LCA, notify USCIS and offer return transportation. STEM OPT: notify the DSO within 5 business days and submit the final I-983 evaluation. Taiwan Art. 9-1 or China non-compete: activate or release.

items.text: Where a separation payment is offered, prepare the agreement from T-SEP-TERMS, allowing for OWBPA or local review periods.
Schedule the exit interview (T-EXIT-INTERVIEW) for regrettable, director-level and flagged exits.
Prepare the local separation documents.
items.detail: US: state separation/UI notices. CA: UI Code 1089 notice, DE 2320 pamphlet, HIPP notice. China: termination certificate. Taiwan: service certificate on request and involuntary separation certificate for Art. 11 exits. India: relieving and experience letters.

items.text: Deliver the confidentiality and IP reminder letter and collect the signed exit certification.
Record rehire eligibility with a reason (OF-10); ER must review before anyone is marked 'not eligible'.
China: complete the personnel-file transfer and the social insurance/housing fund transfer or suspension.
Close the case: all lane tasks done with evidence, documents filed, retention clock set (DS-03).
Calculate final pay: salary to the last day, payable accrued vacation/PTO, commissions, overtime, premiums and expense reimbursements, with lawful deductions only.
items.detail: Vacation payout: CA, CO, IL, MA and others; ON/BC vacation pay; Taiwan unused annual leave; China untaken leave at 300%; India leave encashment.

items.text: Pay final wages by the local deadline.
items.detail: CA: immediately on discharge; on the last day with 72+ hours' notice, otherwise within 72 hours. ON: later of 7 days or next payday. BC: 48 hours (employer ends) or 6 days (quit). India: 2 working days. Taiwan: immediately. China: at termination.

items.text: Do not withhold or deduct final pay for unreturned equipment or incomplete clearance; recover property separately.
items.detail: CA LC 221; India Code on Wages s.18 deduction limits.

items.text: Canada: issue the electronic Record of Employment within 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period.
Taiwan: withdraw Labor, Employment and Occupational Accident Insurance and NHI effective the last day, and report the labor pension stop within 7 days.
Pay deferred statutory amounts: India gratuity within 30 days; Taiwan severance within 30 days; China economic compensation when handover is complete.
Flag the leaver for year-end forms at the updated address: W-2, T4, India Form 130, Taiwan withholding statement.
Enter the termination date in the equity platform; vesting stops under the plan terms.
items.detail: Canada: check whether the award wording clearly excludes the common-law notice period (Matthews); if not, escalate to Legal before cancelling awards.

items.text: Check insider status: Section 16 officers (Form 4 within 2 business days of changes; Form 5 within 45 days of fiscal year-end) and 8-K Item 5.02 for covered officer departures within 4 business days. Remind the leaver that the insider trading policy applies until any MNPI they hold is public.
Send the equity termination statement: vested and unvested awards, exercise window (ISOs 3 months; 1 year on disability), ESPP withdrawal and refund.
China: update the SAFE Circular 7 registration and repatriation of post-exit proceeds. India: confirm TDS on any vest or exercise and remind about Schedule FA.
Executive officers: confirm the clawback acknowledgment survives and no separation term indemnifies recovered amounts.
Confirm coverage end dates and include them in the exit packet.
items.detail: Ontario: benefits continue through the ESA notice period. India: group medical per the package. China: social insurance through the termination month.

items.text: US: notify the COBRA administrator within 30 days of the qualifying event (election notice within 44 days if employer-administered); Cal-COBRA where it applies.
Send life and disability conversion or portability information, FSA run-out and HSA portability details, and the 401(k) distribution and rollover (402(f)) notice.
Close local plans: Canada insurer conversion notices; India PF exit date on the EPFO portal and transfer support; Taiwan NHI withdrawal confirmed.
For flagged departures, review DLP, repository and cloud-upload activity for the prior 30-90 days, and recommend garden leave or cutting access at notice.
Remove access to export-controlled repositories and EDA project areas as soon as handover allows, and record the date for TCP and license records.
Schedule account disablement for the end of D0 (at meeting start for involuntary exits).
Disable SSO, VPN, email, MFA tokens, repositories, EDA license groups and cloud consoles; revoke SSH and API keys; set a 30-day auto-reply and give the manager mailbox access.
Recover and log the laptop, phones and tokens. Remote employees get a prepaid return kit by D-5, with escalation at D+14.
Deactivate badge, lab and cleanroom access; recover lab equipment, samples and keys; clear the desk and locker; update emergency and fire-warden rosters.
Forensically image the devices of flagged departures before re-imaging, and preserve them if a legal hold applies.
Delete or archive accounts on the retention schedule unless a legal hold applies.
Confirm whether the employee is under a legal hold, and send preservation instructions to IT before any device is wiped.
Update the deemed-export license register and TCP records, and meet any license proviso that requires reporting the exit.
Review post-exit restrictions by jurisdiction and choose the right reminder-letter version.
items.detail: CA: no non-compete or non-solicit enforcement. ON: non-competes banned below the C-suite. India: post-exit non-competes void. Taiwan: only with Art. 9-1 compensation. China: activate with monthly compensation or release in writing.

items.text: Approve separation agreement terms, including the SEC Rule 21F-17 and NLRA carve-outs.
For competitor-bound or high-risk departures, send the obligations reminder letter; never threaten to enforce a void restriction.
Section 16 officers: confirm Form 4/Form 5 and any 8-K filings are complete.

notes: D is the last day of employment, not the notice date. For involuntary exits, D-14 to D-1 tasks collapse to the meeting day and access is cut minutes before the meeting.
Never make final pay depend on asset return or clearance (CA LC 221; India's 2-working-day rule). Run clearance in parallel and recover property separately.
A high-risk flag (competitor, customer, PRC-linked entity, controlled-technology access) starts the Security/Legal path (ER-10) at D-14, not D0.
Use one Darwinbox termination record per exit. Each lane closes its own task with evidence (screenshot, receipt, filing number); access-removal evidence supports SOX testing.
Garden leave: remove access on the notice date while pay continues; in Taiwan the employee is still employed and keeps accruing leave.
India's 2-working-day full-and-final rule makes D0 the payroll deadline, not the month-end cycle.
Remote employees: ship return kits by D-5, never hold back pay for late returns, and escalate after D+14.

countryNotes.us: The final-pay deadline follows the work state (e.g., CO and MA same day on involuntary exits; NY and IL next payday). Send state separation/UI notices and COBRA through the administrator; H-1B exits need LCA withdrawal, USCIS notice and a return-fare offer.
countryNotes.us-ca: Pay everything, including accrued vacation, immediately on discharge; on the last day with 72+ hours' notice; otherwise within 72 hours (LC 201-203). Give the UI Code 1089 notice, DE 2320 pamphlet and HIPP notice at separation.
countryNotes.ca: ON final pay is due by the later of 7 days or the next payday; BC within 48 hours (employer ends) or 6 days (quit). Issue the ROE within 5 calendar days after the pay period ends, and continue ON benefits through the ESA notice period.
countryNotes.in: Full-and-final settlement is due within 2 working days of the last working day (Code on Wages s.17(2)), so clearance runs in parallel. Gratuity within 30 days; Karnataka service certificate within 7 days of request; return any original documents.
countryNotes.tw: Settle wages and unused annual leave immediately and severance within 30 days. Withdraw insurance and NHI on the last day and report the pension stop within 7 days; issue the Art. 19 service certificate on request and the involuntary separation certificate for Art. 11 exits.
countryNotes.cn: Issue the termination certificate at exit, pay untaken leave at 300%, and complete the personnel-file and social insurance/housing fund transfer within 15 days. Decide non-compete activation or release in writing.

templates.name: Termination meeting script
templates.purpose: Gives managers and HRBPs a tested structure and exact wording for termination meetings, so they are short, respectful, consistent with the documented reason and legally safe. It covers performance, for-cause and RIF variants, how to handle reactions, and what must happen in the hour after the meeting.
templates.audience: People managers delivering the decision; HRBPs attending as witness and logistics lead; ER and Legal reviewers.
templates.when: Every involuntary termination after approval (OF-02, OF-03). The manager rehearses with the HRBP at least one business day before.
templates.owner: HRBP (preparation and attendance); Employee Relations (script owner)

sections.title: Pre-meeting logistics checklist
sections.intro: Complete every item before the meeting is booked in anyone's calendar.

items.text: The decision is approved at the right level (manager, HRBP and ER; Legal for protected-status, senior or high-risk cases) and the documentation file is complete.
Protected-activity check done: complaints, leave, accommodation requests, pay inquiries, whistleblowing, visa status.
items.detail: CA: retaliation is presumed within 90 days of protected activity. Taiwan: protected periods (maternity leave, occupational-injury treatment). China: LCL Art. 42 categories. India: no dismissal during maternity absence.

items.text: Local ground and process confirmed.
items.detail: China: union notified in writing before a unilateral termination (LCL Art. 43). Taiwan: an Art. 11 or 12 ground, with Art. 12 used within 30 days of learning the facts. India: domestic enquiry and second show-cause completed for misconduct. Canada: ESA and contractual or common-law notice calculated.

items.text: Termination letter ready in the local language: effective date, reason where required, final pay, notice or pay in lieu, benefits end date, equity treatment, documents to follow, contacts.
Final pay ready at the meeting if due then (CA discharge: immediately, including accrued vacation), or scheduled to the local deadline.
Any separation agreement prepared from T-SEP-TERMS; statutory entitlements are not conditional on signing.
Timing set: 10-15 minutes, early in the week, not on a birthday, the eve of a holiday or the day before a vest; a private room near an exit, or a video call.
Roles set: the manager delivers the decision; the HRBP attends as witness and handles logistics. Security is on standby only if there is a credible risk, and is not in the room.
Access cut timed with IT: at the start of the meeting for for-cause or high-risk cases, otherwise right after it. Device return plan or courier kit for remote staff.
Exit packet ready: benefits sheet, equity statement, EAP details, FAQ, HR contact, and a plan for personal belongings.
Team and customer message drafted and approved for release within 2 hours of the meeting.
Thanks for joining. I have some difficult news to share, and I'm going to get straight to it.
Deliver the decision in the first two minutes. No small talk, no preamble about company performance, no 'feedback sandwich'.
Remote meetings: video, with manager and HRBP cameras on. Never by email, chat, text or voicemail.

Over the past [X months] we've discussed specific concerns about [performance area], including on [review / PIP dates]. Despite the improvement plan and the support provided, the required standard hasn't been met.
As a result, the decision has been made to end your employment, effective [date].
This decision is final. [HRBP name] will walk you through your final pay, benefits and next steps.
Local variants
items.detail: Taiwan: cite LSA Art. 11(5), and give Art. 16 notice or pay in lieu plus severance. China: Art. 40(2) only after training or job adjustment and a renewed failure, with 30 days' notice or a month's pay plus N. India (non-workers): the letter cites the contract clause and is non-stigmatic. Canada: this is a without-cause termination; don't call it 'for cause'.

items.text: We've completed our review of [the incident on date / the investigation into specific conduct]. It found that you [specific conduct], which breaches [policy].
Because of how serious this conduct is, your employment is terminated effective immediately.
Use cause language only where Legal confirms the local standard is met.
items.detail: Ontario ESA forfeiture needs wilful misconduct; Taiwan Art. 12 must be used within 30 days; China Art. 39 needs a handbook adopted through democratic procedure; India needs a completed domestic enquiry.

items.text: Don't re-argue the investigation. If the employee raises genuinely new material facts, the HRBP may pause the meeting and consult ER before confirming the decision.
As you know, [Company] is reducing [team / function] because of [business reason]. I'm sorry to tell you that your position is one of those affected.
This is not a reflection of your performance or your contributions.
items.detail: Say this only if it is true for everyone in the group and matches the selection records.

items.text: Your employment will end on [date]. [Until then you'll continue working on X. / You won't be expected to work, but you'll be paid through that date.]
You'll receive a package with the details, including a severance offer. You have [21 / 45 days, or the local period] to review it, and we encourage you to talk to a lawyer before signing.

Deliver every notification in a decisional unit on the same day, one to one; no group video calls. Legal confirms the WARN, Cal-WARN, ON Form 1, BC group notice, Taiwan Art. 33 or China Art. 41 steps before the first meeting.
'Why me?': 'The decision was based on [the documented performance / the selection criteria]. I know this is hard to hear. The decision is final.'

Anger: stay calm and don't match their tone. 'I understand you're upset. [HRBP] will take you through the next steps.' If there are threats or escalation, end the meeting and call Security; never block a doorway.
Silence or shock: pause and offer water and time. 'Take a moment. Would you like me to go through the next steps now, or would you prefer to have them in writing?'
Tears: pause and offer tissues and a few minutes. Don't fill the silence or rush.

A new complaint or allegation: 'I hear that you believe [X]. I'll make sure Employee Relations looks into it.' Record their words and don't debate. Where possible, ER and Legal review it before the effective date.
Negotiation: 'The details are in writing. Please review them and send any questions to [HRBP] within the review period.'

A request to resign instead: answer only with the position agreed in advance, because it affects unemployment benefits and documents (reason codes in Taiwan and China). Never pressure anyone to resign.
Belongings and goodbyes: follow the plan, either escorted collection now or packing and shipping. A farewell email can go out through HR.
Don't say 'This wasn't my decision', 'I fought for you' or 'I'm sorry I have to do this'. It undercuts the decision and suggests someone else had other motives.
Don't refer to age, 'fresh blood', energy, culture fit, family, health, pregnancy, leave, accent, national origin, visa status, or any complaint the employee has made.
Don't give reasons that differ from the documented ones, and don't over-explain; inconsistent reasons are the main evidence of pretext.
Don't promise references, rehire, more severance or help beyond what's approved, and don't discuss other employees.
Don't threaten non-competes, clawbacks or legal action, and never suggest final pay depends on signing anything.
Don't joke, minimize ('you'll land on your feet') or discuss the company's outlook beyond the approved message.
Hand over the letter and packet, asking for a signature acknowledging receipt only, not agreement. China and Taiwan: keep proof that the Chinese version was delivered.
Pay final wages by the local deadline and record the time and method.
Confirm access removal and asset recovery in the offboarding checklist (T-OFFBOARD-CHECKLIST).
Write the meeting note: attendees, times, what was said, reactions, any allegations.
Route any new allegation to ER.
Send the team message: '[Name] is no longer with the company as of today. For [projects], please contact [name].' Give no reasons.

Issue the local documents: CA UI Code 1089 notice and DE 2320; Canada ROE within 5 days of the pay-period end; China termination certificate; Taiwan service and involuntary separation certificates; India relieving letter.
Debrief the manager and remind the team about the EAP.

notes: The script is a floor, not a straitjacket. Managers rehearse it once with the HRBP so the words sound like their own.
The meeting lasts 10-15 minutes. It is a notification, not a discussion; the package and any questions are handled in writing afterwards.
Remote terminations use video with cameras on, a courier kit for devices, and access cut timed with IT. Never use email, chat or voicemail.
The HRBP always attends as witness. In China and Taiwan, deliver the written notice in Chinese and keep proof of delivery; arbitration and labor courts need it.
For RIFs, notify everyone in a decisional unit on the same day in one-to-one meetings. Mass video calls create legal and reputational risk.
No termination may rest on an automated or AI score without documented human review (CA CRD ADS rules).

countryNotes.us: At-will, but the stated reason must match the documentation. Check protected activity and the 180/300-day EEOC charge window, pay final wages by the work state's deadline, and give any state separation notice.
countryNotes.us-ca: Final wages, including accrued vacation, must be handed over at the meeting (LC 201). Give the UI Code 1089 notice and DE 2320; adverse action within 90 days of protected activity is presumed retaliatory.
countryNotes.ca: Not at-will: the letter states ESA notice and severance and any clause-based or common-law entitlement. Avoid a bad-faith manner of dismissal (Honda v. Keays) and use 'cause' language only for proven serious misconduct.
countryNotes.in: Non-workers get a neutral 'termination simpliciter' letter citing the contract clause, not a stigmatic one. Misconduct dismissals only after a domestic enquiry and second show-cause; full-and-final within 2 working days.
countryNotes.tw: The letter must cite the specific LSA Art. 11 or 12 ground, with Art. 12 used within 30 days of learning the facts. Give Art. 16 notice (or pay) and job-seeking leave, and provide a Chinese version.
countryNotes.cn: Written notice citing the LCL article, prior union notification and Chinese-language delivery with proof. Most exits turn into a mutual termination negotiation in this meeting, so the script must not promise terms that haven't been approved.

templates.name: RIF selection matrix & adverse impact review
templates.purpose: Documents how employees were selected in a reduction in force (decisional unit, criteria, weights, scores and evidence) and tests the outcome for adverse impact under privilege before anyone is notified. It also captures the OWBPA disclosure data and the country consultation and notice steps that set the timeline.
templates.audience: HRBPs, business leaders scoring employees, Employee Relations, Legal, HR Analytics.
templates.when: From RIF planning approval to Legal sign-off, before any notification. Re-run if the population or criteria change.
templates.owner: Legal (privilege and sign-off); HRBP (matrix); HR Analytics (statistics)

sections.title: Decisional unit & scope
sections.intro: Complete and date this section before anyone is scored.

items.text: Business rationale
items.detail: One paragraph: the business reason, the cost or scope target, and what work stops or is consolidated. Approved by the function head, FP&A and CHRO, and dated before selection starts.

items.text: Decisional unit
items.detail: The org unit, job family, level band and location(s) within which employees are compared, listing every employee in it. It must match how the decision was actually made; it is the unit disclosed under OWBPA.

items.text: Positions to eliminate
items.detail: Number by job code, level and location: positions, not people.

items.text: Selection date, separation dates and notice-threshold counts
items.detail: Count job losses per site over rolling windows: 30/90 days (WARN, Cal-WARN), 4 weeks (Ontario), 2 months (BC), 60 days (Taiwan MRPA), and the China Art. 41 test of 20 people or 10%.

items.text: Exclusions and rationale
items.detail: Anyone carved out before scoring (e.g., sole owner of a tapeout-critical block, an employee in a statutory protected period). Legal approval required.

items.text: Decision-makers and reviewers
items.detail: Names and roles of the scorers, the independent reviewer (skip-level or peer manager), the HRBP and Legal.

sections.title: Criteria & weights
sections.intro: Weights are illustrative; set them for the business case and fix them before scoring.

items.text: Criterion A: critical skills for the post-RIF roadmap (weight 40%)
items.detail: Define the skill list first (e.g., 3nm physical design sign-off, DDR/LPDDR PHY validation, UVM testbench architecture) and score 1-5 against written anchors.

items.text: Criterion B: performance (weight 30%)
items.detail: Average of the last two completed annual ratings in Darwinbox. No rating created or changed after RIF planning began may be used.

items.text: Criterion C: breadth and versatility (weight 20%)
items.detail: Documented ability to cover the consolidated scope: projects, tools, cross-training.

items.text: Criterion D: fit with the retained roles (weight 10%)
items.detail: How closely the current role matches the roles that remain.

items.text: Tie-breaker
items.detail: Length of service (longer service retained). India 'workers': last-in-first-out within the category unless reasons are recorded. China Art. 41: retain priority groups first.

items.text: Prohibited or high-risk factors
items.detail: Don't use salary cost alone (a proxy for age and tenure), 'potential', 'energy', 'flight risk', leave usage, visa or citizenship status, recent complaints or accommodation needs, or any AI score that hasn't been validated and reviewed by a person.

items.text: Employee ID, job code, level, location, manager, service date
items.detail: Use IDs, not names, in the analysis copy.

items.text: Score for each criterion (1-5), with the anchor it matches
Weighted total and rank within the decisional unit
Evidence reference for each score
items.detail: E.g., rating record, project ownership list, certification. Scores without evidence go back to the scorer.

items.text: Scorer, independent reviewer and calibration date
Legal review flags (not used in scoring)
items.detail: Age 40+, on leave, pending accommodation, open complaint or investigation, protected activity within 90 days, visa holder, statutory protected period (China, Taiwan, India maternity).

items.text: Selected (Y/N), with the reason for any departure from rank order
Redeployment check: open roles reviewed, offered, outcome
items.detail: Expected in practice in Taiwan (last-resort principle) and for China Art. 40(3) consultation; good practice everywhere.

items.text: Date-stamp the criteria and weights memo before any scoring.
Label every draft 'Privileged & Confidential - prepared at the direction of counsel' and keep all versions in the Legal-controlled folder.
Log every change after the first draft: who, what and why.
Keep manager comments factual and evidence-based, with no remarks about age, health, family or commitment.
Keep the full file under the retention schedule: at least 4 years in California, and longer if a claim or charge is filed.
Counsel engages the analyst (HR Analytics or an outside expert) in writing so the work is privileged.
Compute retention rates by age (under 40 vs 40+, plus 50+ and 60+ subgroups), sex, race/ethnicity and national origin (US data only where lawfully held), for each decisional unit and in aggregate.
Four-fifths screen: flag any group whose retention rate is below 80% of the rate for the group with the highest retention.
items.detail: This is a screen, not a safe harbor.

items.text: Test statistical significance: Fisher's exact test for small units, roughly two standard deviations for larger ones; look at practical significance where numbers are tiny.
For each flag, re-check scores and evidence, test alternative selections, and document the business reason for any selection that stands.

Review the effect on employees on leave, recent complainants, visa holders (the Sept 18, 2026 EO makes layoffs a factor in H-1B and LCA adjudication) and CA FEHA categories. Legal signs off before any notification.

sections.title: OWBPA disclosure data (US group program, age 40+)

items.text: Decisional unit: the class, unit or group of individuals covered by the program
Eligibility factors for the program
Time limits: 45 days to consider, 7 days to revoke after signing
Job titles and ages of everyone selected for the program
Job titles and ages of everyone in the same decisional unit who was not selected
Show ages as of a stated date, in a table by job title, with no names. Attach the table to every release in the group and re-issue it if the group changes.

Federal WARN (100+ employees; 60 days for 50+ losses at a site or a qualifying mass layoff) and state mini-WARN laws (NY: 90 days at 50+ employees/25+ losses; NJ: 90 days plus mandatory severance; IL: 75+ employees, 60 days).

Cal-WARN: 60 days' notice for 50+ layoffs within 30 days at a covered establishment (75+ employees), to employees, EDD, the Local Workforce Development Board and local chief elected officials, including SB 617 content.

Ontario: 50+ terminations at an establishment within 4 weeks need 8/12/16 weeks' notice, with Form 1 filed with the Director and posted before notice takes effect. BC: 50+ at one location within 2 months need 8/12/16 weeks' notice to employees, any union and the Minister, on top of individual notice.

India 'workers' with 1+ year of service: 1 month's notice with reasons (or pay in lieu), 15 days' average pay per year of service, notice to the appropriate government, 15 days' wages to the Worker Re-skilling Fund within 10 days, LIFO within category, and a 1-year re-employment preference.

Taiwan: Employment Services Act Art. 33 notice 10 days before separation for each Art. 11 layoff. If Mass Redundancy Protection Act thresholds are met, give the plan to the authority, union or labor representatives and employees 60 days ahead and negotiate within 10 days.

China Art. 41 (20+ employees, or 10%+ of the workforce): explain to the union or all employees 30 days ahead, consider their views, report to the labor bureau (Shanghai: notify worker representatives 30 days before filing from Aug 2026), retain priority groups, and give rehire priority for 6 months. Otherwise use Art. 40(3) consultation or mutual termination.

notes: Build the matrix for each decisional unit before any names are discussed; scorers should not see the Legal review flags.
Keep all statistics under attorney-client privilege and share results orally or in a privileged memo, not in email threads.
The four-fifths rule is a screen, not a safe harbor. Small units need exact tests and a qualitative look at who was chosen.
Don't let cost per head drive selection within a unit; it correlates with age and tenure.
In Canada, selection doesn't change entitlements, but bonus and equity through the notice period (Matthews) drive the cost, so model it per person.
Selection is scrutinized outside the US too: Taiwan's last-resort principle, China's protected categories and India's LIFO rule for workers.
Keep automated scores out of selection unless validated and reviewed by a person (CA CRD ADS rules; 4-year record retention).

countryNotes.us: Group releases for employees 40+ need OWBPA decisional-unit disclosures and 45/7-day periods. Federal WARN applies at 100+ employees plus state mini-WARN laws; run the privileged adverse-impact analysis by age, sex, race and national origin.
countryNotes.us-ca: Cal-WARN counts 50+ layoffs within 30 days at a 75+ employee establishment, regardless of percentage. Analyze FEHA categories, including age 40+ and leave status, and keep ADS data for 4 years.
countryNotes.ca: No statutory selection method for non-union staff, but Ontario mass termination (50+ in 4 weeks) needs Form 1 before notice is effective, and BC group notice (50+ in 2 months) is added on top of individual notice. Human rights codes still apply to the criteria.
countryNotes.in: For 'workers', LIFO applies within each category unless reasons are recorded, along with retrenchment notice to the government and the Worker Re-skilling Fund. Classify every role as worker or non-worker first.
countryNotes.tw: Art. 11 terminations need a genuine business need and documented redeployment consideration, plus the Art. 33 notification 10 days before separation. Mass Redundancy Protection Act thresholds trigger a 60-day plan and negotiation.
countryNotes.cn: An Art. 41 economic layoff (20+ or 10%+) needs a 30-day explanation to the union or employees, a labor bureau report and retention of priority groups. Most MNCs run voluntary mutual-termination programs instead.

templates.name: Separation agreement term sheet (by country)
templates.purpose: A term-by-term checklist for drafting or reviewing separation agreements in each jurisdiction, so the release holds up and no clause breaches whistleblower, labor or local employment law. It separates what is owed regardless from what is offered in exchange for the release.
templates.audience: Employee Relations, HRBPs, Legal, Total Rewards, Stock Admin.
templates.when: Whenever a separation payment is offered in exchange for a release: individual exits, RIFs, mutual separations and executive departures.

sections.title: Global core terms
sections.intro: Apply these to every agreement, then add the country section for the employee's work location.

items.text: Split every amount into (a) owed regardless (final wages, payable accrued leave, statutory notice and severance, vested benefits) and (b) additional consideration offered for the release.
General release of claims, with carve-outs for rights that can't be waived locally.
Protected-rights clause (SEC Rule 21F-17), included verbatim.
items.detail: 'Nothing in this Agreement prohibits or restricts you from filing a charge or complaint with, communicating with, providing information to, or participating in an investigation by the SEC, EEOC, NLRB, OSHA, DOJ or any other government agency, or from receiving an award from a government agency for information provided. You do not need to notify the Company before doing so.'

items.text: No waiver of government whistleblower awards; waiving personal monetary recovery from the Company in agency charges is allowed.
Confidentiality limited to the agreement's terms and amount and to company trade secrets; non-disparagement narrow and, for executives, mutual.
Return-of-property certification, continuing confidentiality and IP obligations, and a reasonable cooperation clause (paid hourly beyond a set number of hours).

Equity: vesting end date, any acceleration and exercise window, with plan documents governing. Payment timing complies with Section 409A: a fixed payment date after the release becomes effective, and a 6-month delay for specified employees.
Executives: the clawback policy (Rule 10D-1) survives, with no indemnity or gross-up for recovered amounts; Compensation Committee approval and an 8-K Item 5.02 review.
Tax withholding, payment schedule, governing law of the work location, entire-agreement clause, counterparts and e-signature.
Local-language or bilingual version where required, and a recommendation to take independent legal advice in every country.

OWBPA (age 40+): plain language, expressly refers to ADEA claims, advises in writing to consult an attorney, 21 days to consider (45 for a group program) and 7 days to revoke after signing; the release takes effect on day 8.
Group programs: attach the decisional-unit disclosure exhibit (from T-RIF-SELECTION).
State that changes to the offer, material or not, do not restart the 21- or 45-day period.
Consideration goes beyond anything already owed (final pay, required vacation payout, vested benefits, NJ mandatory WARN severance).
NLRA (McLaren Macomb): no broad confidentiality or non-disparagement for non-supervisory employees, plus a Section 7 savings clause.
items.detail: 'Nothing in this Agreement limits your right to engage in concerted activity protected by Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act, including discussing terms and conditions of employment.'

items.text: Speak Out Act: carve disclosure of sexual assault and sexual harassment disputes out of the confidentiality and non-disparagement terms.
Exclude non-releasable claims: EEOC and NLRB charge filing, SEC awards, unemployment, workers' compensation, vested ERISA benefits, and FLSA claims without DOL or court approval.

State add-ons: NY (21 days to consider, 7 to revoke, and the complainant's preference before confidentiality of discrimination facts); NJ (no confidentiality of discrimination facts); IL (specific terms for confidentiality of unlawful-practice facts); WA Silenced No More Act.
No non-compete in MN, ND, OK, WY or CA (WA from Jun 30, 2027); rely on confidentiality and, where lawful, targeted non-solicits.
Civil Code 1542 waiver, quoted in full.
items.detail: 'A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party.'

items.text: SB 331 carve-out in any non-disparagement or confidentiality term (Gov Code 12964.5).
items.detail: 'Nothing in this agreement prevents you from discussing or disclosing information about unlawful acts in the workplace, such as harassment or discrimination or any other conduct that you have reason to believe is unlawful.'

items.text: Written notice of the right to consult an attorney and at least 5 business days to do so (OWBPA periods govern for employees 40+).
Pay final wages unconditionally (LC 206.5). Don't release undisputed wages or LC 2802 reimbursement; release workers' comp claims only with WCAB approval.
No no-rehire clause (CCP 1002.5, narrow exceptions), and no confidentiality of facts in filed sexual harassment or discrimination claims (CCP 1001); the amount may stay confidential.
No non-compete or non-solicit (B&P 16600), and no repayment of training, relocation or sign-on costs under AB 692 for agreements from Jan 1, 2026.
Pay ESA amounts unconditionally: notice or pay in lieu, Ontario severance pay (5+ years' service, global payroll test), vacation pay, and benefits continuation through the ESA notice period.
Release consideration above ESA, with the offer positioned against the common-law range, including bonus and equity that would vest during notice (Matthews).
Allow 5-10 business days to review and recommend independent legal advice; consider a legal-fee contribution (C$1,000-2,500).
Structure lump sums as a retiring allowance (withholding 10%, 20% or 30% by amount outside Quebec); check EI allocation; eligible pre-1996 service RRSP rollover (verify).
Plain-language release of human rights claims, signed on an informed and voluntary basis.
Ontario: no non-compete below the C-suite (ESA s.67.2); narrow non-solicits of up to 12 months only.
Quebec remote employees (if any): a French-language transaction under the Civil Code.
Pay statutory dues unconditionally: final wages and leave encashment within 2 working days, gratuity within 30 days, and retrenchment compensation for 'workers'.
Ex gratia (commonly 0.5-1 month's base per year of service, with a 2-3 month floor) is the release consideration; state gross, TDS, net and Form 130 treatment.
Voluntary signature with no coercion: allow 3-7 days and recommend independent advice; use the mutual-separation route for borderline 'workers'.
Relieving and experience letters are never conditional on signing; issue the Karnataka service certificate within 7 days of request.
No post-exit non-compete (Contract Act s.27): garden leave, confidentiality and employee non-solicit only.
Pay stamp duty (Karnataka e-stamp) so the agreement is admissible if it has to be enforced.
Record that the employer proposed the termination (LCL Arts. 36 and 46(2)), which makes N the floor.

Calculate N: one month's wage per full year of service (6-12 months counts as 1 month; under 6 months as half), using the average wage for the prior 12 months including bonuses and allowances, with the 3x local-average-wage cap and 12-year cap for high earners.
items.detail: Market practice for MNC tech employers: N+1 to N+3, often without the cap for senior engineers.

items.text: Itemize N, the +1 pay in lieu where it applies, untaken annual leave at 300%, pro-rata bonus and final wages, with payment dates (compensation is payable when handover is complete).
Social insurance and housing fund: contributions through the termination month, and transfer or suspension within 15 days. Any waiver of social insurance is void.

Non-compete: activate it with monthly compensation (at least 30% of prior 12-month average pay and not below local minimum wage under the MOHRSS 2025 Guidelines; maximum 2 years) or release it in writing now.
Full and final release of labor-dispute claims, confidentiality, handover and a return-of-information certification.
Chinese or bilingual text with Chinese prevailing, signed with the company chop, one copy for each party; issue the termination certificate separately.
Protected employees (pregnancy, medical treatment period, near retirement age): expect materially higher packages, and never apply pressure.
Record an employer-initiated reason code so the involuntary separation certificate supports an Employment Insurance unemployment claim.

Itemize statutory amounts: Art. 16 notice pay, severance (new system: 0.5 month's average wage per year, capped at 6 months; old-system seniority where retained), unused annual leave and pro-rata bonus, plus ex gratia (market 1-3 months).
Settle accrued claims under Civil Code Art. 736; rights under mandatory law can't be waived in advance.
Non-compete only if it meets Art. 9-1 (written, maximum 2 years, at least 50% of average monthly wage paid after exit); otherwise release it.
Provide Traditional Chinese and English versions, and consider recording the settlement in labor mediation for finality.
Pay wages immediately and severance within 30 days; file the Art. 33 notice for Art. 11 layoffs.

notes: This term sheet feeds local counsel-approved templates; don't draft agreements from scratch case by case.
Separating 'owed regardless' from 'offered for the release' is the most common enforceability failure in every country, so show both in the payment schedule.

Use the protected-rights carve-out in every country's template; the SEC treats the restrictive language itself as the violation, and it has charged companies over award-waiver clauses in separation agreements.
Payment timing must be 409A-compliant: a fixed date after the release becomes effective, never 'on signing', so the employee can't choose the tax year.
Executive agreements also need Compensation Committee approval, an 8-K Item 5.02 review, a 280G check in change-in-control cases, and the clawback survival clause.
Keep a version log of templates and of legacy agreements still in force, to support Rule 21F-17 remediation.

countryNotes.us: OWBPA requires 21/45 days to consider plus 7 to revoke, an ADEA reference and written advice to consult an attorney. Include Section 7, agency and SEC-award carve-outs, and respect the Speak Out Act and state NDA limits (NY, NJ, IL, WA).
countryNotes.us-ca: Add the Civil Code 1542 waiver and the Gov Code 12964.5 (SB 331) carve-out with a 5-business-day attorney-consultation notice. No no-rehire clause (CCP 1002.5), and pay undisputed wages unconditionally (LC 206.5).
countryNotes.ca: ESA amounts are paid regardless and release consideration must come on top. Give reasonable review time, recommend independent legal advice, and structure lump sums as retiring allowances.
countryNotes.in: Statutory dues (full-and-final within 2 working days, gratuity within 30 days) can't be made conditional or waived. Ex gratia is paid against a voluntary release, and the agreement should be stamped.
countryNotes.tw: A settlement under Civil Code Art. 736 itemizing statutory amounts plus ex gratia. An employer-initiated reason code preserves unemployment benefits; a non-compete is valid only with Art. 9-1 compensation.
countryNotes.cn: A mutual termination agreement (LCL Art. 36) recording employer initiation, an N-based calculation, SI/HF handling and the non-compete decision, with the Chinese version prevailing. Waivers of social insurance are void.

templates.name: Investigation plan & report
templates.purpose: Plans and documents a fair, prompt and proportionate workplace investigation from intake to closure, producing a report that a decision-maker, regulator or court can rely on. It covers harassment, discrimination, retaliation, misconduct, fraud, trade-secret and export-control allegations.
templates.audience: Employee Relations investigators, HRBPs, Ethics & Compliance, external investigators, Legal.
templates.when: Opened within 2 business days of any triaged allegation that needs fact-finding (ER-01 triage); the plan is set before the first interview.
templates.owner: Employee Relations (with Legal for privileged and Tier 1 matters)

items.text: Case ID, date received, intake channel
items.detail: Channels: hotline or web (anonymous where lawful), manager, HR, exit interview, Legal, external agency.

items.text: Allegation summary in the reporter's words: who, what, when, where, witnesses, documents
Policies potentially breached (POL IDs)
Risk tier
items.detail: Tier 1: senior leader, accounting or securities, export control or sanctions, violence or threats, sexual assault, anything government-facing. Legal-directed, often an external investigator. Tier 2: harassment, discrimination, retaliation, trade secrets. Tier 3: interpersonal and policy issues.

items.text: Routing and statutory body
items.detail: ER; Ethics & Compliance (audit committee reporting under SOX 301); Trade Compliance; Security; India Internal Committee; Taiwan harassment or bullying complaint procedure; Ontario OHSA program.

items.text: Investigator and independence check
items.detail: No reporting line, prior involvement or personal relationship with the parties. Use an external investigator for executives or where HR is implicated.

items.text: Privilege: Legal-directed (Y/N)
items.detail: If yes, every interview opens with an Upjohn warning and drafts are labeled privileged.

items.text: Interim measures
items.detail: Schedule or reporting-line change, paid administrative leave, no-contact instruction, access suspension. Measures must not disadvantage the complainant.

items.text: Scope: numbered allegations to decide, and what is out of scope
Interview list and order
items.detail: Usually the complainant, then witnesses, then the respondent, then follow-ups. Note language needs and any accommodations.

items.text: Documents and data to collect, with legal basis
items.detail: Email, chat, badge logs, repository and DLP logs, CCTV. Basis: policy notice and the Ontario e-monitoring policy, BC PIPA, PIPL notice, DPDP s.7(i) or SPDI Rules, Taiwan PDPA. No access to personal social media (CA LC 980).

items.text: Legal hold issued: date and custodians
Target timeline
items.detail: Tier 2: report within 30 days. India POSH inquiry: 90 days. Taiwan sexual harassment: about 2 months, extendable by 1 (verify).

items.text: Recording and interpreter arrangements
items.detail: Record only with all-party consent (CA Penal Code 632). Use independent interpreters, not colleagues.

items.text: China evidence stays in China unless cross-border transfer rules are met; counsel reviews Counter-Espionage and Data Security Law sensitivities before any transfer.

I'm [name] from [Employee Relations / firm]. I've been asked to look into some concerns, and I haven't reached any conclusions. I'll ask questions and take notes, and you can ask for a break at any time.

(Upjohn warning, if counsel-directed) I'm a lawyer for the Company, not for you. This conversation is privileged, but the privilege belongs to the Company, which may decide to share what you tell me with others, including government agencies.
Please keep what we discuss confidential so the investigation isn't compromised. That doesn't stop you from talking about your own pay or working conditions, or from contacting any government agency.
The Company prohibits retaliation against anyone who raises a concern or takes part in an investigation. If anything happens that feels like retaliation, tell me or the Speak Up line straight away.

Open questions: 'Tell me what happened, in your own words.' 'When and where? Who else was there?' 'What exactly was said or done?' 'Did you tell anyone at the time?' 'Are there messages or documents?' 'Has anything like this happened before?' 'Who else should I speak to?'
Respondent: put each allegation with specifics (date, words, conduct), allow a full response, and ask for any witnesses or documents they want considered.
Share a written summary with each interviewee to confirm or correct. In China and Taiwan, a signed Chinese-language statement strengthens the evidence.
Evidence log: item, source, date collected, collector, chain of custody, storage location
Finding for each allegation: Substantiated / Not substantiated / Inconclusive
items.detail: Standard: preponderance of the evidence (more likely than not).

items.text: Credibility factors
items.detail: Plausibility, corroboration, consistency, motive to falsify, past record. Demeanor alone carries little weight.

items.text: Keep facts, analysis and conclusions separate. State policy findings, not legal conclusions: write 'breached POL-09', not 'harassment under Title VII'.
Executive summary (one page): allegations, findings, policy conclusions
Background, scope and process: dates, interviews, documents reviewed, limitations
Findings of fact and analysis for each allegation, citing the evidence
Conclusions: which policies were or were not breached
Recommendations for the decision-maker
items.detail: Corrective action under ER-04, remediation for the complainant, training, control or process fixes. The investigator doesn't decide discipline.

items.text: Appendices: interview summaries, evidence log, timeline
The decision-maker (not the investigator) decides the action and documents the rationale.
Tell the complainant and respondent the outcome in writing where required (Ontario OHSA: results and any corrective action), without sharing disciplinary detail beyond that.
India POSH: the IC report is due within 10 days of completing the inquiry, the employer acts within 60 days, and the case goes in the annual report.
Taiwan: notify the local authority of the sexual harassment complaint and its result; register bullying cases in MOL's reporting system.
Hold retaliation check-ins with the complainant and key witnesses at 30 and 90 days.
Close the case in case management, report SOX-relevant matters to the audit committee quarterly, and apply the retention schedule.

notes: The investigator is never the decision-maker; keeping the roles apart protects both the process and the outcome.
Run Tier 1 matters at the direction of counsel: Upjohn warnings, privileged labels on drafts, and counsel deciding what is shared.
Document every step when it happens, and write the report for an outside reader: a judge, the HRTO, a PRC arbitration commission or a labor authority.
Keep confidentiality instructions narrow (Stericycle, Rule 21F-17): never bar talking to agencies or discussing pay and working conditions.
Local statutory bodies take precedence where they exist: India's Internal Committee, Taiwan's complaint procedures (with external members for bullying cases where required), Ontario's OHSA program.
In trade-secret and insider cases, coordinate with Security before interviewing the respondent so evidence is preserved and forensic images are taken first.
Keep China evidence in China where possible, and use PIPL-compliant notices for any personal data collected.

countryNotes.us: A prompt, impartial investigation is the core Faragher/Ellerth defense. Title VII and state laws still cover sexual orientation and gender identity despite the EEOC's rescission of its 2024 guidance, and SOX-related complaints go to the audit committee.
countryNotes.us-ca: Investigate under 2 CCR 11023 with trained, impartial investigators; don't access personal social media (LC 980). Recording needs all-party consent (Penal Code 632), and claimants have 3 years to file with the CRD.
countryNotes.ca: Ontario's OHSA requires an appropriate investigation of every harassment complaint and written results to both parties; an inspector can order a third-party investigation at the employer's cost. BC requires procedures aimed at fully addressing the incident.
countryNotes.in: Sexual harassment complaints by women go to the Internal Committee: inquiry within 90 days, report within 10 days, employer action within 60 days, confidentiality under s.16. Misconduct dismissal needs a domestic enquiry that follows natural justice.
countryNotes.tw: Sexual harassment: take immediate corrective measures, investigate impartially and notify the local authority of the complaint and result. Bullying (from 1 July 2026): investigation committees with at least half external members where required, and registration in MOL's system.
countryNotes.cn: Collect only necessary data under a PIPL notice, and keep evidence in China unless transfer rules are met. Signed Chinese-language statements strengthen arbitration evidence; brief counsel on Counter-Espionage and Data Security Law sensitivities.

templates.name: Performance improvement plan
templates.purpose: Documents specific performance gaps, measurable success criteria, support and a timeline, so the employee has a genuine chance to improve. It also creates the record that local law expects before any performance-based exit (Taiwan's last-resort principle, China LCL Art. 40(2), US and California pretext scrutiny).
templates.when: When documented coaching hasn't closed a sustained gap, typically after at least one documented feedback conversation and 30+ days. Not during protected leave or while an accommodation request is pending.

items.text: Employee, ID, job title and level, manager, HRBP, work location (country/state)
Start date, mid-point review date, end date
items.detail: Default 60 days; 30 days only for narrow, well-documented gaps; 90 days for senior or complex roles. Taiwan and China: at least 60 days recommended.

items.text: Prior feedback: dates of documented conversations, last rating, coaching already given
items.detail: At least one documented feedback conversation should come before a PIP.

items.text: Confirmation that the issue is performance, not conduct
items.detail: Misconduct goes through corrective action (ER-04), not a PIP.

items.text: HRBP pre-check: no pending accommodation request, protected leave or complaint in the last 90 days. If the gap may be health-related, start the interactive process (T-ACCOMMODATION) first.

Local mapping: Taiwan Art. 11(5) needs objective standards, training and redeployment consideration; China Art. 40(2) needs training or job adjustment before a renewed failure; in India, check worker status; in Canada, a PIP doesn't create cause.

sections.title: Performance gaps
sections.intro: Up to three gaps. Each must be specific, observable and tied to the expectations for the role's level.

items.text: Gap 1: expectation
items.detail: What the role requires, citing the level guide or goals (e.g., 'An IC3 physical design engineer closes timing on assigned blocks within the schedule').

items.text: Gap 1: observed performance, with examples
items.detail: Dates, deliverables and metrics, e.g., 'Missed 3 of 5 timing-closure milestones on block X between March and May; two floorplan re-spins were needed.'

items.text: Gap 1: impact
items.detail: Effect on schedule, quality, customers or the team.

items.text: Gap 2: expectation, observed performance, impact
Gap 3: expectation, observed performance, impact (optional)
Behavioral expectations, if any (e.g., design-review participation, responsiveness), with examples
Measurable success criteria for each gap
items.detail: E.g., 'Close DRC/LVS clean on blocks A and B by [date] with no more than one review cycle each.' A fully performing peer must be able to meet them within the period.

items.text: Support the company will provide
items.detail: Training, a mentor, reduced scope, lab or compute time, weekly 1:1s.

items.text: Obstacles or resources the employee identifies
Redeployment or alternative roles considered
items.detail: Expected in practice in Taiwan and China; good practice elsewhere.

items.text: Unattainable or shifting criteria look like pretext. Don't add criteria mid-plan without HRBP approval and a reset end date.
Weekly check-in: date, progress on each criterion (On track / Partial / Not met), evidence, manager comments, employee comments
Mid-point review: date, and the written summary shared with the employee
Plan changes: date, reason, HRBP approval
Final review meeting: date and summary
Outcome: Completed successfully / Extended once (up to 30 days) / Not met
Next step if not met
items.detail: Redeployment, a role change (in China and Taiwan this needs consent or must follow the LSA Art. 10-1 transfer principles), or termination through the local process (OF-02) with HRBP and ER approval.

items.text: Pay and rating effects during the plan
items.detail: E.g., merit increase or promotion deferred under policy; bonus per the plan terms.

items.text: After successful completion, sustained performance is expected. A recurrence within 6 months goes to written corrective action rather than a new PIP.
This plan sets out clearly what's expected and the support you'll get. I want you to succeed, and we'll meet every week to review progress together.
Employee comments (optional; a written response may be attached)
Signatures and dates: employee (acknowledging receipt, not agreement), manager, HRBP; language version used
items.detail: Chinese version for Taiwan and China; keep proof of delivery.

items.text: If the employee declines to sign, write 'Delivered on [date]; employee declined to sign' and have a witness initial it.
The plan is not a contract. In the US it doesn't change at-will employment; elsewhere it doesn't replace statutory process. Store it in the restricted Darwinbox folder.

notes: A PIP must be a real chance to succeed. If the exit decision is already made, have a separation conversation instead (consider mutual separation outside the US).
Keep performance and conduct separate; conduct goes through corrective action.
Default to 60 days: 30 only for simple, well-documented gaps, 90 for senior or complex roles.
Compare with how peers with similar gaps were treated. Inconsistency is the main pretext evidence, and US employers should review PIP outcomes quarterly for adverse impact (Muldrow).
Metrics from automated or AI tools need human review before they go into a PIP (CA CRD rules; IL HB 3773 notices).
HRBP approval is required before delivery, and ER approval before any termination for failing to meet the plan.

countryNotes.us: At-will, but a PIP is the core evidence against pretext. Check protected activity and FMLA, ADA and PWFA status, and don't treat completing the PIP as a promise of continued employment.
countryNotes.us-ca: Adverse action within 90 days of protected activity is presumed retaliatory (LC 98.6, 1102.5). Start the FEHA interactive process first if the performance issue may be disability-related.
countryNotes.ca: Poor performance rarely amounts to just cause. The PIP supports fairness and a without-cause decision, but ESA and common-law notice still apply; avoid pay or role changes that could be constructive dismissal.
countryNotes.in: There is no statutory PIP. For non-workers, termination simpliciter must be non-stigmatic; for 'workers', document a fair process and consider mutual separation to avoid Tribunal risk.
countryNotes.tw: Before an Art. 11(5) incompetence dismissal, courts expect objective standards, coaching or training, a genuine improvement plan and redeployment consideration. Up to 10 sick days a year cannot affect the evaluation.
countryNotes.cn: Art. 40(2) needs proof of incompetence against communicated standards, then training or job adjustment, then a renewed failure. The standards must be in the handbook or contract and acknowledged in Chinese.

templates.name: 30/60/90-day onboarding plan
templates.purpose: A sequenced checklist from offer acceptance to Day 90 that makes a new hire, especially an engineer, compliant, safe and productive: paperwork and right-to-work first, export clearance before controlled access, safety training before lab access, and design tools ready on Day 1. It also sets 30/60/90 goals and probation checkpoints.
templates.audience: Hiring managers, new hires, buddies, People Ops, IT, Trade Compliance, EHS, Facilities, Immigration.
templates.when: From offer acceptance to Day 90; tasks are generated in Darwinbox from the hire transaction.
templates.owner: Hiring manager (plan and goals); People Ops (compliance steps)

items.text: Create the hire in Darwinbox from Greenhouse: start date, location, manager, cost center, position ID.

Export-control check for flagged job codes: collect U.S.-person status and citizenship/permanent residency on the separate export form (never with the I-9). Trade Compliance decides whether a license is needed; start date and access depend on clearance.
Background check completed under local rules: FCRA and CA Fair Chance steps; India BGV consent; China PIPL consent; Taiwan PDPA notice.

Contract and IP paperwork signed before any access: CA PIIA with LC 2870 and DTSA notices; Canadian contract with termination clause and IP assignment before Day 1; India appointment letter and stamped agreement; China labor contract; Taiwan Chinese-language contract.

Work authorization confirmed: US visa start-date buffers (H-1B, L-1, TN, OPT); Canadian work permit; Taiwan work permit or Gold Card; China work permit, Z visa and residence permit within 30 days of entry.
Laptop or Linux workstation and VDI configured for the role; accounts created but disabled until Day 1; hardware shipped to remote hires by Day -3.
Request design tool licenses (synthesis, place-and-route, simulation, formal, sign-off, layout), the license-server group and compute quota.
Order the badge; queue lab and cleanroom access pending safety training.
Assign a buddy (same team, 1+ year tenure) and send a welcome email with the Week 1 schedule.
Complete local Day 1 compliance.
items.detail: US: I-9 Section 1 on Day 1 and Section 2 within 3 business days. CA: SB 294 notice and emergency-contact designation. Ontario: ESA poster and required policies within 30 days. India: EPF Form 11/UAN and nominations. Taiwan: labor insurance and NHI effective Day 1. China: social insurance and housing fund registration within 30 days.

items.text: Policy acknowledgments: Code of Conduct, insider trading policy (pre-clearance and blackout rules), confidentiality, acceptable use and monitoring notice, privacy notice (CCPA, PIPL, DPDP/SPDI, PDPA), and the local handbook or work rules.
Welcome 1:1: role expectations, team charter, how design reviews work, draft 30/60/90 goals.
Enable SSO, MFA, email and chat; complete security awareness training.
Technology Control Plan briefing and signed acknowledgment for flagged roles; grant access only to repositories cleared for the individual's export status.
Buddy walkthrough: repository structure, version-control workflow, regressions and CI, bug tracker, design-review calendar.

Lab safety orientation before any lab access: ESD, chemical hygiene, lasers, high voltage, emergency procedures (CA IIPP/HazCom; Taiwan OSH new-hire training; Ontario basic OHS awareness; BC orientation before starting work).
Benefits and equity: enrollment window (US typically 30 days), equity grant summary, ESPP enrollment dates.
Enter the 30/60/90 goals in the Darwinbox performance module.
