Complete mandatory training: harassment prevention (CA within 6 months), POSH (India), AODA (Ontario), insider trading, export-control awareness, trade secrets and data handling, anti-bribery.
Deliver a starter task (e.g., fix a lint or CDC issue, add a regression test, run a block through synthesis).
Meet key stakeholders: architecture, verification, physical design, DFT, software, product, foundry liaison.
Enable badge, lab and license-server access once training is recorded; arrange cleanroom gowning at partner sites if needed.
Complete the Day 30 pulse survey (T-ONBOARD-PULSE).
30-day check-in: are expectations clear, are tools, licenses and access sufficient, and what is blocking progress?
Assign an owned deliverable (a block, test plan, feature or bring-up task) with review milestones.
Present work at a design or code review.
Review access against need and remove temporary broad access (least privilege).
Probation checkpoint.
items.detail: China: probation length depends on the contract term (maximum 6 months), and a probation dismissal needs written criteria and evidence before it ends. India: 3-6 months with a confirmation letter. Taiwan: probation is not a free exit. Canada: ESA notice starts after 3 months. US: no 'permanent after probation' wording.

items.text: Document the 60-day check-in in Darwinbox.
Own the deliverable end to end, including tapeout or release checklist items.
Day 90 review: goals met, partly met or not met, with written feedback and a development plan.
Issue the probation outcome letter where probation is used (India confirmation; China before probation ends).
Complete the Day 90 pulse survey.
Mark onboarding complete in Darwinbox and send quality-of-hire feedback to TA.

notes: Access depends on need and export status. The export form sits outside the I-9 process and is seen only by Trade Compliance.
EDA licenses are expensive and pooled, so request them 10 days before start and plan compute quotas with the license admin.
No lab or cleanroom access until a safety training record exists.
In China, probation dates are legal dates (one probation per employer, maximum length set by the contract term), so HR calendars them from Day 1.
Remote hires need hardware shipped early and remote bench or VDI access instead of lab time.
Adjust the pace: interns and new graduates need a longer ramp; senior hires should get a stakeholder map before their first deliverable.

countryNotes.us: Form I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days (E-Verify where required and for STEM OPT), state new-hire reporting within 20 days, and a PIIA with the DTSA notice signed before any access.
countryNotes.us-ca: SB 294 notice and emergency contact at hire, the LC 2810.5 notice for non-exempt hires, harassment training within 6 months, and IIPP/HazCom/WVPP safety onboarding with SB 513 training records.
countryNotes.ca: Contract (termination clause, IP assignment, moral-rights waiver) signed before Day 1. Ontario: new-hire information, ESA poster and disconnecting/e-monitoring policies within 30 days, plus AODA training; BC: new-worker orientation before starting work.
countryNotes.in: Appointment letter, EPF Form 11/UAN (EPF ceiling INR 25,000 from 17 Sep 2026), gratuity and PF nominations, maternity benefit information for women, POSH induction. Karnataka bars keeping original certificates.
countryNotes.tw: Enroll Labor, Employment and Occupational Accident Insurance and NHI effective Day 1, and report pension within 7 days. Distribute the filed work rules and harassment/bullying channels, and deliver OSH training for new hires.
countryNotes.cn: Labor contract signed by Day 1 (never later than one month), SI/HF registration within 30 days, handbook acknowledgment, separate PIPL consents for sensitive data and cross-border transfer, SAFE Circular 7 for equity grantees, and written probation criteria.

templates.name: New-hire pulse survey (Day 30 & Day 90)
templates.purpose: A short (5-7 minute) pulse at Day 30 and Day 90 that catches onboarding failures while they can still be fixed and measures early-tenure attrition risk. Results drive manager follow-up and fixes to IT provisioning, licensing and export-clearance cycle times.
templates.audience: All new hires, including interns on assignments of 8+ weeks and rehires. Results go to HRBPs, managers (aggregate), People Ops, IT and Trade Compliance (themes only).
templates.when: Sent automatically from the survey platform on Day 30 and Day 90 after start; open for 7 days with one reminder. Items marked 'Day 30 only' or 'Day 90' are shown in that wave.

Close the loop: the HRBP reviews low scores (2 or below on manager or role items) with the manager within 5 business days, without identifying respondents.
Keep it short (about 30 items) and use skip logic to hide lab and tool items from non-engineers.
Translate into Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) and Simplified Chinese (China); English works for India and Canada.
Join responses to HRIS demographics only through HR Analytics under privacy controls; never report on individuals.
Track 'job matches what was described' and 'see myself here in two years' at Day 90; together they predict first-year attrition.

countryNotes.us: Keep participation voluntary and avoid questions that draw out medical or disability information. Comments may include NLRA-protected discussion of working conditions, so never try to trace authors.
countryNotes.us-ca: Give a CCPA notice at collection covering survey data and retention; identified follow-up requests are personal information subject to access and deletion rights.
countryNotes.ca: BC PIPA requires notice of the purpose for collecting employee personal information; disclose survey-vendor processing in the employee privacy notice.
countryNotes.in: Rely on the SPDI Rules privacy policy until DPDP duties start on 13 May 2027; keep participation voluntary and collect only what is needed.
countryNotes.tw: Give a PDPA notice at collection, don't ask for sensitive data such as health information, and provide a Traditional Chinese version.
countryNotes.cn: Give a PIPL notice, and obtain separate consent if identifiable responses are transferred to a US survey platform; provide a Simplified Chinese version.

templates.name: Structured interview scorecard
templates.purpose: The standard scorecard for every interview in a structured loop: set questions per competency, an anchored 4-point scale and evidence-based notes submitted before the debrief. It reduces bias, makes decisions defensible and keeps interviewers away from prohibited topics.
templates.when: Every interview in the loop; submitted in Greenhouse within 24 hours and before the debrief.
templates.owner: Talent Acquisition (template and training); Hiring manager (competencies and questions)

items.text: Candidate ID (Greenhouse), requisition ID, role and level
Interview stage and format
items.detail: Recruiter screen / technical screen / onsite loop / panel / hiring manager; onsite or video.

items.text: Interviewer and assigned competencies
items.detail: Each interviewer covers 2-3 competencies from the interview plan; no two interviewers cover the same one.

items.text: The interviewer has completed structured-interview training in the last 24 months.
Onsite candidates get no lab tours, code demos or screen shares of controlled technology unless Trade Compliance has cleared them (deemed-export risk).

sections.title: Competencies & questions
sections.intro: Ask the core questions as written, for every candidate for the role. Follow-ups may vary; the core question may not.

items.text: Technical depth: 'Walk me through the microarchitecture of a block you designed. What were the main trade-offs between timing, area and power, and how did you decide?'
items.detail: Look for concrete numbers, alternatives considered, and what they would change now.

items.text: Problem solving (standard exercise): 'Here is a failing simulation log / timing report. Talk me through how you would debug it.'
items.detail: Use the same artifact for every candidate at the level, and score the approach, not just the answer.

items.text: Quality mindset: 'How did you decide a block was verified well enough to tape out? What coverage or sign-off criteria did you use?'
Collaboration: 'Tell me about a time you disagreed with an architect or another team about a spec. What did you do, and what happened?'
Ownership: 'Tell me about something you owned that slipped. What happened, and what did you change afterwards?'
Learning agility: 'Describe a new tool, flow or domain you had to learn quickly. How did you get up to speed?'
Communication: 'Explain [a concept from your recent work] as you would to a product manager.'
Integrity: 'Tell me about a time you raised a concern about quality, safety or compliance. What did you do?'
Domain module from the interview plan: the analog/mixed-signal, physical design, DFT, firmware or post-silicon validation question set.
Never ask for, and stop a candidate from sharing, a prior employer's confidential information (designs, code, customer names, roadmaps, yields). Note it on the scorecard if it happens.
Rating for each competency (no midpoints)
items.detail: 1 Strong no: clear gaps or significant concerns. 2 No: below the bar for the level. 3 Yes: meets the bar for the level, with evidence. 4 Strong yes: exceeds the bar, with evidence of next-level scope.

items.text: Evidence for each competency
items.detail: What the candidate said or did (quotes, specifics), not impressions such as 'smart' or 'good fit'.

items.text: Concerns or risks, with evidence
Level supported by the evidence (e.g., IC3 vs IC4)
Submit in Greenhouse before the debrief and before talking to other interviewers.

Don't ask about age or graduation year, national origin or accent, citizenship, marital or family status, pregnancy or childcare plans, religion, disability or health, union membership, caste, horoscope or blood type.
items.detail: For flagged roles the recruiter asks the single approved export-control question; interviewers never ask about citizenship.

items.text: Don't ask about current or past pay (banned in California, 20+ other US states and cities, and BC). Only the recruiter asks about pay expectations.
No questions about criminal history; checks happen after a conditional offer where fair-chance laws apply.
If a candidate asks for an accommodation, pass it to the recruiter; don't evaluate or discuss the request.
Use AI note-takers or scoring tools only if TA and Legal have approved them (NYC LL 144, IL HB 3773, Ontario posting disclosure, CA ADS rules).
Overall recommendation: Strong no / No / Yes / Strong yes
Summary rationale (3-5 sentences, based on evidence)
Recommended level, with the relevant scope and experience evidence (no pay history)
Debrief record (hiring manager): decision, dissenting views, tie-break reasoning
Scorecard submitted within 24 hours of the interview.
Ontario: every interviewed applicant is told whether a hiring decision was made within 45 days of their last interview.

notes: Every candidate for a role gets the same core questions; the Greenhouse interview plan assigns competencies to interviewers.
Use the anchored 4-point scale with no 'maybe', and submit independently before the debrief to avoid anchoring on the loudest voice.
Write evidence, not impressions. Scorecards are discoverable and subject to CCPA and PIPL access requests.
The hiring manager can't override the panel without a documented rationale in the debrief record.
Monitor stage pass-through rates for adverse impact (Title VII 703(k)), without making decisions based on demographics.
Clean-hire rule: stop candidates who start volunteering confidential prior-employer information, and note that it happened.

countryNotes.us: No salary-history questions where banned (20+ states and cities), criminal history deferred under fair-chance laws, and AI rules (NYC LL 144, IL HB 3773) if tools score interviews. Export-control questions come only through the approved recruiter script.
countryNotes.us-ca: No salary history (LC 432.3), no criminal history before a conditional offer (Gov Code 12952) and no cannabis questions (Gov Code 12954). ADS used in interviews falls under CRD rules, with 4-year record retention.
countryNotes.ca: Human-rights-compliant questions only (no age, family status or place of origin; in Ontario, also no citizenship). Ontario: disclose AI use in postings and tell interviewed candidates the outcome within 45 days; BC: no pay-history questions.
countryNotes.in: Avoid questions on caste, religion, marital or pregnancy status and HIV status, and offer disability accommodation in interviews under the RPwD Act.
countryNotes.tw: Employment Services Act Art. 5 bars questions on marital status, pregnancy plans, horoscope, blood type and non-job-related private information (fines NT$300,000-1,500,000).
countryNotes.cn: No questions to women about marriage or childbearing plans and no gender, ethnicity or religion criteria. Give a candidate privacy notice and get PIPL consent before reference calls.

templates.name: Offer approval matrix

It keeps offers within pay-transparency ranges, delegated equity authority and Compensation Committee oversight.

sections.title: Base salary position in range
sections.intro: Thresholds are illustrative; calibrate them to your ranges and budget, and review annually against the Compensation Committee's delegation.

items.text: Base at or below the range midpoint for the level and location
items.detail: Approver: Hiring Manager; the recruiter confirms the range in Greenhouse. SLA: same day.

items.text: Base above the midpoint, up to the 75th percentile of the range
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + Total Rewards partner. SLA: 1 business day.

items.text: Base above the 75th percentile, up to the range maximum
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + Total Rewards + HRBP, with an internal-equity check against incumbents at the same level and location.

items.text: Base above the range maximum
items.detail: Approvers: VP + Head of Total Rewards; attach market data and the internal-equity analysis. Check the posted range is still a good-faith estimate (CA SB 642) and update postings if needed.

items.text: Level or title differs from the approved requisition
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + HRBP. Re-price against the new level's range and re-post if the range changes.

items.text: Sign-on up to 10% of base

items.text: Sign-on above 10% and up to 25% of base, or buyout of a forfeited bonus

items.text: Repayment terms
items.detail: CA: no stay-or-pay repayment for agreements from Jan 1, 2026 (AB 692), apart from narrow standalone discretionary-bonus terms. India: reasonable, pro-rated liquidated damages only. China: repayment only under service-period (training) agreements. Taiwan: minimum-service terms only under Art. 15-1. Prefer forward-vesting cash.

items.detail: Approvers: Hiring Manager + Total Rewards. Granted on the next scheduled grant date under the Equity Grant Policy.

items.text: Equity above guideline, up to 150%
items.detail: Approvers: VP + Head of Total Rewards.

items.text: Equity above 150% of guideline, or buyout of unvested equity from a prior employer
items.detail: Approvers: CHRO + CFO, within the pool delegated by the Compensation Committee.

items.text: Any grant above the delegated authority limit, and any grant to a Section 16 officer
items.detail: Approver: Compensation Committee.

items.text: Grants are made only on pre-set grant dates and never timed around MNPI. PRC grantees need SAFE Circular 7 registration; India, Taiwan and China use country sub-plan terms; Canadian award wording must address the notice period.
Standard relocation package tier

items.text: Relocation above the tier, or a lump sum above policy
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + Mobility + Total Rewards.

items.text: Immigration sponsorship (H-1B, L-1, TN, green card commitment, GTS/LMIA, Taiwan or China work permit)
items.detail: Approvers: Immigration + Dept Head. Trade Compliance completes the I-129 Part 6 export certification for US petitions.

items.text: Hire in a state or country with no existing entity or payroll registration
items.detail: Approvers: People Ops + Payroll + Legal + Tax (registration and permanent-establishment risk).

items.text: Non-standard severance, guaranteed bonus or accelerated vesting
items.detail: Approvers: CHRO + General Counsel.

items.text: Changes to the standard PIIA, restrictive covenants or governing law
items.detail: Approver: Legal. California, Ontario, India, Taiwan and China limits apply.

items.text: Candidate is a relative of an employee, director, government official or customer employee, or was referred by an official
items.detail: Approvers: Ethics & Compliance + Legal (FCPA 'princeling' review and related-person check).

items.text: Candidate joining from a direct competitor or an Entity List-linked company
items.detail: Approvers: Legal + Security, through a clean-hire review before the offer.

items.text: Role requires an export license for this candidate
items.detail: Approver: Trade Compliance. The offer states that the start date or access depends on authorization.

items.text: Start date more than 90 days out, or rescinding an accepted offer
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + HRBP + Legal. In China an accepted offer is a binding pre-contract commitment.

items.text: VP offers (non-officer)
items.detail: Approvers: CEO + CHRO.

items.text: Executive officer or Section 16 officer offers
items.detail: Approver: Compensation Committee (base, target bonus, equity, severance and change-in-control terms), with input from its independent consultant.

items.text: Inducement grants outside a shareholder-approved plan
items.detail: Approved by the independent Compensation Committee or a majority of independent directors, with a press release on the material terms (Nasdaq 5635(c)(4)).

items.text: Officer disclosure and onboarding
items.detail: 8-K Item 5.02 within 4 business days where required; Form 3 within 10 days; clawback acknowledgment; insider trading pre-clearance set-up.

items.text: Related-person check (Item 404) for offers to immediate family of directors or executive officers where pay exceeds $120,000.
All approvals are captured in the Greenhouse offer approval chain; no email or chat approvals.
No numbers are shared with the candidate, even verbally, before approval.
The country offer template is used: California-compliant; Canadian with termination clause; India appointment letter; China labor contract; Taiwan Chinese version.
Approval SLA of 1 business day per level; the recruiter escalates after 2.
Quarterly audit of above-midpoint offers and exceptions by function, fed into the pay equity review (CO-06).

notes: Approvals are by role, not by named person; record delegates in Greenhouse when approvers are away.
Offers above the posted range weaken the good-faith basis of the range; update the posting or document why the exception is one-off.
Check internal equity against incumbents at the same level and location before any above-midpoint offer, so new-hire pay doesn't create gaps that CO-06 has to fix later.
Equity grant timing belongs to the Equity Grant Policy: fixed grant dates, no backdating, no timing around earnings.
Re-approve any change after approval, including start date, level, location or equity mix.
Revisit the thresholds each year alongside the salary structure refresh and the Compensation Committee's delegated authority.

countryNotes.us: Executive officer pay goes to the Compensation Committee of independent directors and may need 8-K Item 5.02 disclosure within four business days. Inducement grants need independent approval and a press release (Nasdaq 5635(c)(4)).
countryNotes.us-ca: Offers must stay within a good-faith posted range (LC 432.3, SB 642) and use California templates with no non-compete or non-California forum clause (LC 925) and no stay-or-pay repayment (AB 692).
countryNotes.ca: The offer and contract (with an ESA-compliant termination clause and equity wording covering the notice period) must be signed before start. Ontario public postings limit ranges to a C$50,000 spread.
countryNotes.in: The offer must be followed by a statutory appointment letter at joining. Structure CTC so 'wages' are at least 50% (this drives PF and gratuity cost); joining-bonus clawbacks are valid only as reasonable liquidated damages.
countryNotes.tw: The approval should show which wage components count as 'wages' for severance, and the cost of any Art. 9-1 non-compete compensation. Provide a Traditional Chinese contract.
countryNotes.cn: An accepted offer is a binding pre-contract commitment, so rescinding it costs damages. Equity for PRC employees needs SAFE Circular 7 registration, and the labor contract must be signed by Day 1.

templates.name: Policy document template
templates.purpose: The standard structure for every HR policy in the library, so policies are consistent, testable, localizable and auditable. It builds in what regulators and courts look for: clear scope, an owner, approval, version control, country addenda and a protected-rights carve-out.
templates.audience: Policy owners, the HR Policy & Governance lead, Legal reviewers, translators.
templates.when: When creating a new policy or making a material revision, and at each scheduled review under DS-08.
templates.owner: HR Policy & Governance (template); each policy owner (content)

items.text: Policy ID and title
items.detail: Format POL-NN; the title as it appears in the policy register.

items.text: Policy owner (function and role)
Approver(s)
items.detail: E.g., CHRO + General Counsel; a Board committee where required (clawback, insider trading, code of conduct).

items.text: Effective date
Version number
Review cycle and next review date
items.detail: Annual, or every 2 years plus on any change in law.

items.text: Applies to
items.detail: Entities, countries and worker types (employees, interns, contingent workers, directors).

items.text: Classification and available languages
items.detail: Internal or public; English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese and any others.

items.text: Supersedes (prior policy IDs and versions)
Purpose
items.detail: 2-3 sentences on the risk or objective the policy addresses and why it matters.

items.text: Scope
items.detail: Who and what is covered, by entity, location and worker type.

items.text: Exclusions
items.detail: What is out of scope, and where it is covered instead.

items.text: Definitions
items.detail: Capitalized terms used in the policy. Where the policy implements a law, use the statutory definition and say so.

items.text: Keep policy statements (what) separate from procedures (how), and link procedures by process ID.
Policy statements
items.detail: Numbered, testable statements ('The Company will...', 'Employees must...') with thresholds, timelines and approvals. Use 'must' for requirements; don't write 'should' when you mean 'must'.

items.text: Roles and responsibilities
items.detail: Employees, managers, HR, Legal, the policy owner and any committee.

items.text: Speak Up and non-retaliation (standard text)
items.detail: '[Company] does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who in good faith raises a concern, reports a possible violation or takes part in an investigation. Retaliation is itself a violation of this policy.'

items.text: Protected rights (standard text)
items.detail: 'Nothing in this policy prohibits you from reporting possible violations of law to, filing a charge with or communicating with any government agency (including the SEC, EEOC, NLRB, OSHA or a local labor authority), taking part in a government investigation, receiving a government award, or discussing wages and working conditions with co-workers. You do not need to notify the Company.'

items.text: Consequences of violation
items.detail: Corrective action up to and including termination, consistent with local law and work rules.

items.text: Training and acknowledgment
items.detail: Who must acknowledge the policy and how often (at hire, annually, on material change), tracked in the LMS.

items.text: Procedures
items.detail: Process IDs that implement the policy (e.g., ER-02 Workplace investigation).

items.text: Exceptions
items.detail: Who may approve them, the documentation required and the maximum duration; exceptions are logged in the policy register.

items.text: Related documents
items.detail: Other policies, standards, forms and templates (e.g., POL-02, T-INVESTIGATION).

items.text: Records and retention
items.detail: Records the policy creates, their system of record and the retention period under the schedule.

items.text: Questions and contacts
items.detail: The policy owner's mailbox and the Speak Up line.

sections.title: Country addenda
sections.intro: An addendum adds or changes only what local law requires; write 'No addendum needed' where that is true. Where an addendum is more protective, it prevails.

items.text: United States (federal and multi-state)
California
Canada (Ontario, British Columbia)
India
Taiwan
China

Local enforceability steps are part of approval: China's democratic procedure and acknowledgments; Taiwan work-rules filing at 30+ employees; India standing orders or service rules; Ontario written-policy deadlines.
Version history table: version, date, author, summary of changes, approver
Approval record: name, title, date, e-signature
Legal review completed for each in-scope country.
Translations completed and checked, with the governing-language version identified.
China: evidence of democratic procedure on file (employee congress or all-employee consultation, union consultation, publication and signed acknowledgments).
Taiwan: work rules filed with the local labor authority (the Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park sites) and posted.
Ontario: copies given to employees within 30 days where the ESA requires (disconnecting from work, electronic monitoring) and kept for 3 years after the policy stops applying.
Published to the policy portal, prior version archived, and the acknowledgment campaign launched in the LMS.

notes: One policy, one owner. Policy statements say what; procedures (processes) say how. Don't mix them.
Write provisions as testable statements that an auditor could check.
Add country addenda only where local law requires something more or different, and say 'No addendum needed' explicitly elsewhere.
Local enforceability steps (China democratic procedure, Taiwan work-rules filing, India standing orders) are part of approval, not an afterthought; without them the policy can't support discipline.
Every policy that touches confidentiality or reporting carries the protected-rights carve-out.
Keep the version log for the life of the policy plus the retention period; Rule 21F-17 remediation needs traceability of legacy versions.
Some policies must be public or filed: the Code of Conduct (Nasdaq 5610), insider trading policy (10-K Exhibit 19) and clawback policy (Exhibit 97).

countryNotes.us: Handbook policies must meet Stericycle with a Section 7 savings clause, handbooks must describe FMLA rights (50+ employees), NY requires a written harassment policy, and the Nasdaq 5610 code must be public.
countryNotes.us-ca: The EEO/harassment policy must list all FEHA categories and be translated into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce (2 CCR 11023). The CCPA notice must state retention periods.
countryNotes.ca: Ontario employers with 25+ employees need written disconnecting-from-work and e-monitoring policies by March 1, copies within 30 days and 3-year retention; OHSA harassment and violence policies are reviewed annually. Quebec requires French.
countryNotes.in: Standing orders (300+ workers) or equivalent service rules are needed, and statutory abstracts and POSH IC details must be displayed in English and Kannada or Telugu.
countryNotes.tw: At 30+ employees, policies affecting terms of employment must be in work rules filed with the local labor authority within 30 days and posted; the Traditional Chinese version governs.
countryNotes.cn: Rules affecting vital interests are enforceable only after democratic procedure (employee congress or all employees), union consultation and publication with signed acknowledgment (LCL Art. 4). The Chinese version prevails.

templates.name: Stay interview guide
templates.purpose: A structured, manager-led conversation to learn what keeps valued employees and what might pull them away, before they resign. It produces a short individual action plan and themes for the team.
templates.audience: People managers (who conduct it), HRBPs (who coach and aggregate), skip-level leaders.
templates.when: Annually for all direct reports, with critical talent first; also 60-90 days after a reorg, manager change or peer exits. Never in the same meeting as performance or pay decisions.

items.text: Prioritize top performers, critical skills (e.g., analog/mixed-signal, physical design sign-off, DFT, post-silicon validation), succession-slate members and teams hit by reorgs, manager changes or peer exits. Aim to cover every direct report each year.
The manager conducts the interview, not HR. The HRBP gives first-time managers a 15-minute prep session.

Review the context privately: tenure, last rating, compa-ratio, time since last promotion, next equity vest and refresh history, any internal applications. Don't use this data to negotiate in the meeting.
Schedule 30 minutes at least 4 weeks away from performance reviews and comp decisions.
Send the invitation: 'I'd like 30 minutes to hear what keeps you here and what might make you think about leaving. It's not a review, and there's nothing to prepare.'
This isn't a performance conversation. I want to understand what's working for you, what isn't, and what I can do to make this a place you want to stay.
I can't promise to fix everything, but I'll be honest about what I can do, and I'll follow up within a month.
Start with the easiest question and let them talk. Aim to listen 80% of the time and keep notes brief.

sections.title: Core questions
sections.intro: Pick 5-7 questions; you don't need all of them. Follow the employee's energy.

items.text: What do you look forward to most when you start your work week?
What are you learning here, and what do you want to learn in the next year?
What would make your job more satisfying?
How are your workload and schedule, including tapeout crunches and late calls across time zones?
Do you have the tools, licenses, lab time and compute you need?
Do you feel recognized for your work? How do you like to be recognized?
How can I be a better manager for you? What should I start or stop doing?
If you could, what would you change about how our team works?
What might tempt you to leave?
items.detail: Probe gently: recruiter approaches, types of roles or companies, and what those roles offer that this one doesn't.

items.text: When did you last think about leaving? What prompted it?
Where do you want your career to go, and what next step do you want here? By when?
items.detail: Probe: clarity of promotion criteria, scope, technical versus management track, internal moves.

items.text: How do you feel about how you're paid, including equity?
items.detail: Listen and explain the process (ranges, review cycle, refresh grants). Don't disclose others' pay or promise changes; flag a suspected market gap to Total Rewards.

items.text: What one thing, if it changed, would make you more likely to be here in two years?
Make no offers or promises in the meeting. Requests about pay, promotion or a retention bonus go through the HRBP and the off-cycle or counteroffer process (CO-05).

Don't ask about retirement plans, family plans, health or other personal circumstances. If the employee raises them (e.g., caregiving), focus on work arrangements and point them to HR and the leave policies.

If the employee raises harassment, discrimination, retaliation, safety or ethics concerns, stop and route them to Employee Relations within 1 business day, as in the exit interview allegations protocol.
Never use what you hear against the employee, for example by dropping them from a project because they mentioned thinking about leaving. It destroys trust and can be retaliation.
Don't ask for details of outside offers or pressure the employee to disclose them.
Top three things that keep the employee here
Top three risks that could pull them away, and overall risk: Low / Medium / High
Agreed actions, each with an owner and due date
items.detail: E.g., a project rotation, a mentor, a promotion-readiness plan, a request for a pay review, a flexibility change.

items.text: Items to escalate (Total Rewards, HRBP, skip-level)
Follow-up date (within 30 days) and next stay interview (in 6-12 months)
Log a short summary in Darwinbox, visible only to the manager, skip-level and HRBP. The HRBP aggregates themes quarterly for HR Analytics.

notes: Manager-led builds trust and accountability; an HR-led stay interview feels like an audit.
Follow-up is the point. Commit to one or two actions you can actually deliver, and report back within 30 days.
Keep stay interviews separate from pay and performance conversations so they don't turn into negotiations.
Aggregate themes feed engagement action planning (EN-01) and talent reviews (PD-05).
Train managers to listen: a handful of good questions and silence beat a complete questionnaire.
Notes are personal data: restricted access, and retention under the schedule.

countryNotes.us: Employees may discuss pay and working conditions (NLRA Section 7), so never discourage it. Avoid questions about retirement plans (ADEA risk).
countryNotes.us-ca: Employees may disclose their wages and request the pay scale for their role (LC 432.3). Don't ask about off-duty conduct or for access to personal social media.
countryNotes.ca: BC prohibits reprisal for discussing pay. A promise made in a stay interview (e.g., a promotion or retention bonus) can become an enforceable term, so put commitments in writing only after approval.
countryNotes.in: Notice periods of 60-90 days and frequent counteroffers mean retention risk shows early. Run any retention bonus through policy, with reasonable, pro-rated clawback only.
countryNotes.tw: When discussing pay timing, allow for TSMC and MediaTek profit-sharing and bonus cycles. Don't record sick-leave use as a risk factor (2026 rules bar adverse treatment for up to 10 days a year).
countryNotes.cn: Hold the conversation in Mandarin. Retention commitments that change pay or role need written agreement (LCL Art. 35), and stay-interview notes are personal information under PIPL.

templates.name: Accommodation request & interactive process log
templates.purpose: Records every step of a good-faith interactive process for disability, pregnancy, religious and other accommodation requests, from the first request to review. The log shows that options were explored in good faith; failing to engage is itself a violation in California and Canada.
templates.audience: HRBPs and Leave & Accommodation specialists, managers, EHS, Legal.
templates.when: Opened when an employee or applicant asks, in any words, for a change at work for a medical, pregnancy, religious or family-status reason. Reviewed at least every 6 months while an accommodation is in place.

items.text: Request date and how it was received (employee, manager, HR, applicant via recruiter)
Employee or applicant name, ID, role, location, manager
Basis of the request
items.detail: Disability or medical condition; pregnancy, childbirth or lactation; religion or creed; family status (Canada); victim of violence (CA); other.

items.text: What the employee is asking for, in their words
items.detail: No diagnosis is needed. Record the functional need (e.g., 'can't stand for more than 30 minutes').

items.text: Job functions affected
items.detail: List the essential functions from the job description and which of them the limitation affects.

items.text: Preferred language and any representative (union, advocate, family member)
Interim measures in place while the process runs
Any expression of need is a request; no magic words or form are required. Acknowledge within 2 business days. A manager who hears a request must tell HR the same day.
Is documentation needed? (Y/N) and why
items.detail: Only when the need or limitation isn't obvious. Under the PWFA, don't ask for documentation for common pregnancy modifications such as water, extra breaks, sitting or standing, or lactation.

items.text: What was requested and from whom
items.detail: Functional limitations, expected duration and how the change would help; never the diagnosis or full medical records.

items.text: Dates requested and received
Where it is stored
items.detail: A separate confidential medical file, not the personnel file, restricted to Leave & Accommodation staff. Health data is sensitive: it needs consent or a statutory basis under PIPL (separate consent), Taiwan PDPA and India's SPDI Rules/DPDP.

items.text: Meeting 1: date, attendees, options discussed, employee's suggestions, company's suggestions, next steps
Follow-up meetings: the same fields
Options considered
items.detail: For each option: description, effectiveness, cost, operational impact, decision and reason.

items.text: Consultations
items.detail: EHS (lab or chemical exposure, reproductive hazards), IT (assistive technology), Facilities (ergonomics, lab benches), the manager, Legal (undue hardship).

items.text: Lab and cleanroom roles
items.detail: Hazard assessment for pregnant or post-partum employees; offer reassignment or controls rather than forced exclusion (PWFA, FEHA). Taiwan maternal health rules apply; in China, no overtime or night shifts from 7 months of pregnancy.

items.text: Days from request to decision (target 15 business days)
items.detail: Delays count against good faith, so record the reason for any delay.

items.text: Accommodation granted: description, start date, temporary or permanent, review date
Alternative offered, and why the requested option wasn't chosen
items.detail: An effective alternative is enough, but document why.

items.text: Denial or undue hardship analysis
items.detail: US: significant difficulty or expense (for religion, substantial increased cost under Groff v. DeJoy). Canada: undue hardship is a high bar (cost, health and safety). Legal must approve any denial.

items.text: Leave as an accommodation
items.detail: Considered after other options; coordinate FMLA/CFRA/PDL, Ontario ESA or local leave through LV-01.

items.text: Written decision sent to the employee (date), and how to raise concerns or ask for reconsideration
Implementation owner and completion date recorded (equipment ordered, schedule changed, remote arrangement documented).
Manager briefed on what to provide, without medical details.
Check in at 30 days and whenever circumstances change; reopen if the accommodation isn't working.
Monitor for retaliation: ER reviews any adverse action within 90 days of the request before it happens.
Ontario (50+ employees): document an individual accommodation plan and return-to-work process under the AODA.
Close the case and set retention (California 4 years; follow the schedule elsewhere).

notes: Start the process on any sign of need. A manager who hears 'my back makes sitting all day hard' has received a request.
Keep medical information in a separate restricted file; managers get functional needs only.
The accommodation must be effective, not necessarily the one preferred, but document why an alternative was chosen.
For lab and cleanroom roles, involve EHS in chemical and reproductive-hazard reviews, and offer reassignment rather than forcing exclusion.
Applicants are covered too, including accommodations for AI or automated assessments (CA CRD rules, Ontario AODA).
Track time to decision; unexplained delays undermine the good-faith record.

countryNotes.us: The ADA and PWFA (15+ employees) require an interactive process. The PWFA limits documentation for common pregnancy modifications, and undue hardship for religious accommodation means substantial increased cost (Groff v. DeJoy).
countryNotes.us-ca: Failing to engage in a timely, good-faith interactive process is a separate FEHA violation (Gov Code 12940(n)). Cover pregnancy (PDL), religion and requests arising from AI/ADS assessments, and keep records for 4 years.
countryNotes.ca: The ON and BC Human Rights Codes require accommodation of disability, family status and creed to the point of undue hardship. Ontario employers with 50+ employees need documented individual accommodation plans and a return-to-work process under the AODA.
countryNotes.in: The RPwD Act 2016 requires reasonable accommodation and a published equal opportunity policy, and establishments with 20+ employees appoint a liaison officer. Health data is sensitive personal data and needs consent.
countryNotes.tw: Maternal health protection requires hazard assessment and job adjustment for pregnant and post-partum (1 year) workers, with a written program at 100+ worker sites or for hazardous work. Health data needs written consent or a statutory basis under the PDPA.
countryNotes.cn: Female employee special protections apply (no overtime or night shifts from 7 months of pregnancy, nursing breaks), and medical treatment period rules govern illness. Health data is sensitive PI that needs separate consent and a PIPIA.

templates.name: Requisition justification form
templates.purpose: Captures why a role is needed, what it costs, how it is leveled and which compliance flags (export control, sponsorship, pay transparency, classification) apply before a requisition opens in Greenhouse. It gives FP&A and HR one approval record tied to the headcount plan.
templates.audience: Hiring managers (authors), HRBPs, FP&A, Total Rewards, recruiters, Trade Compliance.
templates.when: Before any requisition is opened or any agency is briefed; for backfills, as soon as a resignation is accepted.
templates.owner: Hiring manager (author); FP&A and HRBP (approval); Talent Acquisition (workflow)

items.text: Requisition type: new headcount / backfill / conversion (contractor to employee) / intern
Job title, job code, job family and level (from the job architecture)
Department, cost center, hiring manager, HRBP, recruiter
Work location(s) and remote eligibility
items.detail: Country, state or province, and city. Location sets the pay range, posting rules, classification, payroll registration and notice rules.

items.text: Employment type and contract term
items.detail: Regular full-time / part-time / fixed-term / intern. Taiwan: fixed-term only for temporary, short-term, seasonal or specific-project work. China: note the contract term, which sets the maximum probation. India: fixed-term employees get pro-rata gratuity after 1 year.

items.text: Number of openings and target start date
Business need
items.detail: What work, for which product or program (e.g., 'verification lead for the N3 SoC tapeout in Q2'), and what happens if the role isn't filled.

items.text: Why now, and alternatives considered
items.detail: Redistributing work, internal transfer, a contractor (check classification rules), automation, deferral.

items.text: Backfill details
items.detail: Departing employee, exit date, and whether the scope or level should change.

items.text: In the approved headcount plan? (Y/N)
items.detail: If not, the funding source or offset.

items.text: Outcomes expected in the first 12 months
Pay range for the level and location, and the posting range
items.detail: From Total Rewards. The posting range must be a good-faith estimate (CA SB 642; Ontario spread of C$50,000 or less; BC and US state rules).

items.text: Budgeted base, target bonus, equity guideline, sign-on, relocation and agency fee
Fully loaded annual cost (from FP&A)
Classification
items.detail: US FLSA and state exempt tests (California: salary floor plus duties). India: worker or non-worker by dominant duties. Taiwan: no salary-based exemption. China: standard hours or approved special hours.

items.text: Export control: will the role access EAR/ITAR-controlled technology or source code? (set by Trade Compliance)
items.detail: A flag triggers the separate export screening process. Postings may not say 'US citizens only' unless a law, regulation or government contract requires it.

items.text: Immigration sponsorship likely? (Y/N)
items.detail: Drives H-1B cap timing and cost, I-129 Part 6, Canadian GTS or ICT routes, and Taiwan or China work permits.

items.text: Security clearance required by a government contract? (Y/N)
items.detail: The only common basis for a citizenship requirement.

items.text: Lab or safety-sensitive work? (Y/N)
items.detail: Triggers EHS training, and pre-employment or occupational health exams in Taiwan and China.

items.text: Candidate referred by a customer, government official or partner? (Y/N)
items.detail: Routes to Ethics & Compliance for anti-corruption review.

items.text: Job description reviewed: requirements are job-related, with no age limits, gender or marital-status criteria or 'Canadian experience', and any degree requirement is justified.
AI screening tools to be used? If so, disclosures are configured (Ontario postings, NYC LL 144, Illinois) and bias testing is on file (CA ADS rules).
Local posting steps done: India vacancy notification to the career centre; Taiwan salary range where pay is under NT$40,000 a month.
In-plan backfill at the same level
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + FP&A. SLA: 2 business days.

items.text: In-plan new headcount
items.detail: Approvers: Dept Head + FP&A + HRBP (level and org design) + Total Rewards (range).

items.text: Out-of-plan headcount, a higher level on a backfill, or a conversion
items.detail: Approvers: VP + FP&A lead + CHRO.

items.text: VP-level and above
items.detail: Approvers: CEO + CHRO; officer roles also go to the Compensation Committee at offer stage.

items.text: Position ID created in Darwinbox and linked to the Greenhouse requisition, with approval dates recorded.
Requisitions open for more than 60 days are reviewed for scope, level and range.

notes: Backfills aren't automatic. Re-examine scope and level every time; a departure is the cheapest moment to reshape a team.
Location decides the law: posting range, classification, final pay and notices. Confirm entity and payroll registration before approving a remote hire in a new state or country.
Set the export-control flag at the requisition, not at offer, so screening is uniform, job-based and non-discriminatory.
Never put 'US citizens only' in a posting unless a documented legal or contract requirement exists.
Fix the range and level before sourcing; changing them mid-search needs re-approval and an updated posting.
Tie every requisition to a Darwinbox position ID so headcount and payroll controls (SOX) reconcile.

countryNotes.us: Many states require pay ranges in postings, including for remote roles (CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, NJ, VT, MA, VA, ME, CT and others). Export-control flags must not become citizenship screens (8 U.S.C. 1324b).
countryNotes.us-ca: Every posting that could be filled in California needs a good-faith base pay range (LC 432.3, SB 642). Confirm exempt status against the $70,304 (2026) salary floor and the duties tests.
countryNotes.ca: Ontario postings (25+ employees) must show pay with a spread of C$50,000 or less, disclose AI use, say whether a vacancy exists and drop 'Canadian experience'. BC postings must include pay.
countryNotes.in: Classify each role as worker or non-worker by dominant duties at the requisition stage (this drives retrenchment rights, standing orders and the GRC), and notify vacancies to the career centre under the SS Code rules.
countryNotes.tw: Use indefinite-term contracts for ongoing roles and fixed-term only for temporary or project work. Postings for pay under NT$40,000 a month must show the salary range.
countryNotes.cn: Remove gender, marital or childbearing, ethnicity and age criteria from job descriptions, and decide the contract term and probation length (which depends on the term) at the requisition stage.
